issues.summary: Filter chips reset to default after switching workspaces
description: On the main dashboard, chip filters (status, assignee, component) are remembered while you stay in one workspace. After you change workspace from the top switcher, every chip snaps back to the product default set even though the prior selection was still valid for that board.

Expected: each workspace keeps its own chip selection for the browser session, or at least restores the last filters stored under that workspace id. Actual: the chip bar always reloads from DEFAULT_FILTERS after a workspace change, discarding custom combinations of three or more chips.

Suspect the filter store keys only on userId and never includes workspaceId, so the hydrate path after workspace.switched overwrites local state with the global default map. Users who juggle two or three workspaces re-apply the same chips dozens of times per day and lose the filtered board context mid-review.
comments: Reproduced on a dual-workspace account: chips for In Progress + my assignee survive a hard refresh in workspace A, then vanish the moment I switch to B and back.
Looking at DashboardFilterProvider — the persist call writes to nimbus.filters.v2 without scoping. Drafting a key of nimbus.filters.v2:${workspaceId} and a migration for the unscoped blob.

issues.summary: Dashboard chart legend overlaps axis labels on 1280px viewports
description: Throughput charts on the overview dashboard look fine at 1440px and above. At exactly 1280px wide (common laptop layout with the left nav open), the legend pills sit on top of the Y-axis tick labels and make both unreadable.

You should still be able to read every tick and every series name without overlap. What happens is the legend is absolutely positioned against the chart container while the axis padding stays fixed at 32px, so once the plot area shrinks the two regions collide.

Likely the chart layout pass computes legend height after axis margins are locked, instead of reserving space first. Support has two tickets from teams that live on 13-inch displays and cannot read weekly velocity at that breakpoint.
comments: Confirmed at 1280x800 with the nav expanded; at 1279px the legend wraps under the chart and the clash disappears.
Chart kit is Recharts 2.12 — checking whether margin.left needs to grow when legend.payload.length > 4, or if we should force legend to bottom under 1366px.

issues.summary: Billing invoice PDF downloads with a blank second page
description: Monthly invoice PDFs generated from Billing → Invoices open correctly on page one (header, line items, totals) but always include a second page that is completely blank except for the footer page number.
A single-page invoice should produce a single-page PDF. Accounting users who archive invoices into their ERPs end up with empty pages that their OCR tools flag as corrupt or incomplete.

Hypothesis: the PDF renderer always appends a page-break after the totals block because the template still contains a residual page-break-after: always on .invoice-totals from when multi-page tax schedules were required. Removing that rule or gating it on content height over 720pt should drop the empty page.

issues.summary: Auth session cookie is not refreshed after silent token renewal
description: Silent access-token renewal succeeds (network tab shows 200 from /auth/token/refresh with a new expires_at), yet the session cookie nimbus_sid keeps its original Max-Age and Expires values from the first login.

After renewal the cookie should be re-issued with a sliding window matching the new token lifetime. Instead the browser keeps the old cookie; once that clock runs out the next navigation returns 401 even though a valid access token still sits in memory.

Root cause candidate: the refresh handler updates the in-memory JWT store but never calls Set-Cookie on the response when the grant type is refresh_token. Only the interactive login path sets the cookie. Users on long-lived tabs hit sudden logouts about 12 hours after the first sign-in despite continuous silent renewals.
comments: Happens more often on tabs left open overnight; morning navigation always bounces to login even though the refresh call ran at 02:14.

issues.summary: Notification toast stacks behind the sticky editor toolbar
description: When the sticky editor toolbar is pinned (scrollY > 64), success and error toasts from save, share, and permission actions render underneath the toolbar instead of above it. Clicks on toast actions never register because the toolbar captures pointer events.
Toasts should sit in a layer above chrome UI. Currently toast z-index is 40 while the sticky toolbar uses 50, so any toast that appears near the top of the viewport is fully or partially obscured.

Stacking context is created by the toolbar's position: sticky plus transform used for the shadow fade. Raising the toast portal to z-index 60 (or moving it outside the editor stacking root) should fix it. Missed confirmations are especially painful on failed share invites where the error is invisible.
comments: Easiest repro: open a long doc, scroll until the toolbar sticks, trigger Share with an invalid email — the red toast is half-hidden under the toolbar.
Portal already mounts on document.body; the sticky bar still paints over it. Will bump toast layer and add a regression snapshot at sticky=true.

issues.summary: Editor autosave writes the previous document revision every third save
description: Editor autosave should always persist the latest document body. On every third successful autosave (approximately every 90 seconds with default debounce), the payload sent to PUT /docs/{id}/revisions contains the body from the previous revision instead of the live editor state.

Expected: each autosave captures the current ProseMirror doc. Actual: saves 1 and 2 are correct; save 3 rewrites the server copy with revision N-1 content, wiping the intervening edits until the next good save.

Cause was a ring buffer of size 2 in AutosaveQueue that rotated the wrong index when flush and enqueue raced after a 2s idle. The third flush reused the stale snapshot reference. Fix re-reads view.state.doc at flush time instead of caching the JSON string at enqueue.
Impact was silent data loss for anyone typing through multiple autosave cycles; several writers reported that their last paragraph vanished after returning from a short break.
comments: Instrumented autosave in staging: every third POST body matched revision_id of the prior row in document_revisions.
Root cause confirmed in AutosaveQueue.rotate — off-by-one on writeIdx when length hit capacity 2.
Patch landed: flush always serializes from the live editor view. Integration test runs 9 consecutive autosaves and asserts body equality.
Verified on production canary for 48h; no mismatched revision pairs in the autosave audit log.

issues.summary: Workspace switcher shows stale plan tier until full page reload
description: The workspace switcher dropdown shows the plan tier badge (Free, Team, Business) next to each workspace name. After an admin upgrades or downgrades a workspace, the badge in the switcher keeps showing the old tier until the user does a full browser reload.

Plan changes should surface within a few seconds of the billing webhook completing. In practice the switcher reads from a bootstrap payload cached at login and never refetches GET /workspaces/me after workspace.plan_changed.
Stale tier text causes people to open the wrong upgrade CTA or believe a paid feature is unavailable. Caching the tier on the workspace list without a subscription to plan events is the likely gap.

issues.summary: Dark mode contrast fails WCAG AA on secondary dashboard metrics
description: In dark theme, secondary dashboard metrics (cycle time subtitle, percentile footnotes, compared-to-last-period deltas) use #8B8B9A on #1A1A24. Measured contrast is about 3.1:1, below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for normal text.
Those labels must meet AA in both themes. Primary numbers are fine; only the secondary line fails. Light mode already passes at 5.2:1.

Token color.text.muted was tuned for light backgrounds and reused as-is for dark. Splitting a color.text.muted.dark near #B0B0C0 or lifting the dark muted step one level should clear the audit without washing out the hierarchy.
comments: axe DevTools flags 6 nodes on the overview page when prefers-color-scheme is dark.

issues.summary: Mention autocomplete inserts an extra space before the handle
description: Typing @ in the editor opens mention autocomplete. Choosing a person inserts @handle but with an extra leading space when the caret was already after a space, producing two spaces before the at-sign.

Insertion should replace the trigger query with a single mention node and at most one separating space from the preceding word. The double space shows up in rendered comments and in notification previews as an awkward gap.

Mention plugin insertMention always prepends a space text node for word boundary, ignoring that the delete range already consumed a trailing space from the query. Reopened after the first fix only covered mid-word triggers, not triggers that start after punctuation-plus-space.
comments: Originally fixed for mid-sentence mentions; automation passed.
QA reopened: still doubles when you type space then @ at the start of a new sentence after a period.
Still broken on build 2026.07.18 — inserting after Hello[space] yields Hello[space][space]@maya. The space-normalization branch never runs when $from.parentOffset is already a hard break plus space.

issues.summary: Kanban column counts ignore cards moved via keyboard shortcuts
description: Kanban column headers show a live card count. Dragging a card with the mouse updates both source and destination counts immediately. Moving a card with keyboard shortcuts (Focus card then Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Arrow) updates the card position but leaves the header counts unchanged until a full board refresh.
Counts should stay consistent regardless of input method. Keyboard moves go through board.moveCard which updates column arrays but skips the columnMeta.counts reducer that the drag-end path calls.

Teams that rely on keyboard navigation for accessibility see wrong WIP totals and sometimes pull more work into a column that already looks full by count. Aligning the keyboard path with the same count mutation as pointer drag should close the gap.
comments: Reproduced with VoiceOver and keyboard only: count on Ready stayed at 7 after I moved two cards into In Progress.
moveCardKeyboard action is missing the recalculateColumnCounts side effect. Wiring that in now.

issues.summary: Date picker shifts one day backward in Pacific/Auckland timezone
description: Users with browser timezone Pacific/Auckland who pick a calendar date on dashboard filter widgets (due date, created range) get a stored ISO date one calendar day earlier than the day they clicked.
Selecting 15 March should store 2026-03-15. Instead the control emits 2026-03-14T11:00:00.000Z and the chip displays 14 March after reopening the picker.

Conversion runs Date.UTC(y, m, d) after reading local Y/M/D, but an intermediate new Date(y, m, d) is serialized via toISOString() before the UTC rebuild, which shifts the day for UTC+12/+13 offsets. Building a plain date string YYYY-MM-DD without a Date instance until the API boundary would avoid the skew.

issues.summary: Export CSV truncates multi-line description fields at 255 characters
description: Board and issue CSV exports cut multi-line description fields at 255 characters even when the source field holds several kilobytes. Single-line short descriptions export in full.
Full description text should appear in the CSV cell with embedded newlines escaped per RFC 4180. Importers downstream lose acceptance criteria and repro steps that live past the 255th character.

Export worker still applies a legacy VARCHAR(255) style truncate from the old MySQL report schema; the truncate happens in CsvRowMapper.mapDescription before quoting. Removing that cap or raising it to the same 32KB limit as the API would match product expectations.
comments: Customer on the Business plan attached a sample: description length 1842 chars in the UI, 255 in the CSV column.
Confirmed mapper has substring(0, 255) with a comment about legacy report width. Safe to drop for v2 export.

issues.summary: Sidebar badge count freezes after dismissing the last unread item
description: The sidebar notifications badge shows the unread count. Opening the panel and dismissing the final unread item clears the list UI, but the badge number stays at 1 (or whatever it was) until logout or hard reload.
Badge should hit zero when unread drops to zero. The dismiss mutation removed the item from the list query but never wrote unreadCount: 0 into the badge cache entry.
Stale badge makes people keep opening an empty inbox. Fix was to invalidate notifications.unreadCount on every mark-read/dismiss and to derive the badge from that query only.
comments: Repro: three unreads, dismiss all, list empty, badge still shows 3.
React Query had two keys: list vs count. Dismiss only touched list.
Shipped invalidation on dismiss and mark-all-read; badge now zeroes immediately in staging.

issues.summary: Billing portal redirect loops when the customer already has a portal session
description: From Billing settings, Manage payment methods should send the user to the hosted billing portal once. If the customer already has an open portal session created in the last ~30 minutes, our backend still requests a new session URL, then the portal responds with a redirect back to our return_url, which immediately requests another session — an infinite loop between app and portal.
Expected: reuse the active portal session or show an in-app message that a portal tab is already open. Actual: browser spins until the tab is killed; some users report 20+ hops in a few seconds.

Session create endpoint ignores billing_portal_sessions.active for the customer id and always POSTs a fresh session. Portal then rejects the duplicate with a redirect to return_url without a session token, and our page treats that as needs portal again. Short-circuit when an unexpired session row exists.
comments: Saw this on a sandbox customer that clicked Manage twice quickly; loop only starts when the first session is still active.

issues.summary: Editor collaborative cursors jump to line zero after a paste of 500+ lines
description: In a multiplayer editor session, remote collaborative cursors jump to line 0 (document start) immediately after any participant pastes a block of roughly 500 lines or more. Local caret stays correct; only remote presence positions break.

Remote cursors should re-map through the same transform as the paste transaction. After a large paste they all collapse to position 0 until the next small edit, which confuses co-authors about who is where.

Presence positions were mapped with a stepwise transform walk that bailed out when the step count exceeded 256, returning a null map that defaulted to 0. Raising the limit and batching paste as a single ReplaceStep fixed the jump.
comments: Reproduced with two browsers: paste a 600-line log dump, other user's caret flies to the title.
Presence mapper hit the 256-step guard and returned empty mapping.
Fix: treat large paste as one step for presence remap; verified with 2k-line paste in dogfood.

issues.summary: Saved view filters apply only the first three selected components
description: Saved views on the dashboard can include multiple component filters. When a view is saved with four or more components selected, only the first three are applied when the view is loaded; the rest are silently dropped from the active filter state (though still visible as selected in the edit dialog until save).
All selected components should participate in the query. Boards filtered by four components show a superset of cards because the fourth filter never reaches GET /issues.

The saved-view JSON schema used components as a fixed string array of length 3 from an early product limit. The UI allowed more selections but serialization truncated with slice(0, 3). Schema and mapper now accept up to 25 components.
comments: Customer saved view Platform + API + Mobile + Infra only filtered Platform/API/Mobile.
Confirmed slice in SavedViewSerializer — leftover from when the product capped component filters at three.
Deployed schema bump; re-saved views keep all components. Backfill script rewrote 412 views that had been truncated.

issues.summary: Notification preferences toggle reverts after navigating away within 2 seconds
description: On Notification preferences, flipping a channel toggle (email, in-app, mobile) shows the optimistic ON/OFF state, but if the user navigates to another settings section within about two seconds the toggle reverts to the previous value on return. Waiting longer than two seconds before navigating persists correctly.

A successful preference change should survive navigation immediately. The PATCH to /users/me/notification-preferences is debounced at 2000ms; unmounting the form aborts the debounced write without a flush.
Reopened: the first patch flushed on unmount for email toggles only; in-app and mobile still use a shared debounce timer that is cleared in cleanup without invoking the pending callback.
comments: Initially thought it was cache only; network tab shows the PATCH never leaves if you leave under 2s.
Shipped unmount flush last sprint for email — still broken for push and in-app. Reopening with repro on mobile push toggle.

issues.summary: Dashboard heatmap cells render transparent under forced colors mode
description: Dashboard activity heatmaps look correct in normal themes. Under Windows forced colors / high-contrast mode (or forced-colors: active), every cell paints fully transparent so the grid is an empty frame with axis labels only.

Cells must remain distinguishable in forced colors, typically via system color pairs (Canvas / Highlight) or explicit forced-color-adjust handling. Currently fill comes from CSS variables that resolve to transparent when the browser overrides the palette.

Heatmap cells set background-color to var(--heat-n) without a forced-colors fallback, and forced-color-adjust: none was never set. Adding system-color borders and a non-transparent fallback fill restored the grid for high-contrast users.
comments: Reproduced with Windows 11 contrast theme Aquatic in Edge 128.
Cells had zero computed background in forced-colors; stroke was also cleared.
CSS fix in heatmap.module.css ships with forced-colors media queries; a11y review signed off.

issues.summary: OAuth callback lands on the root dashboard instead of the deep-linked board
description: Starting OAuth from a deep link such as /boards/42?card=881 should return the user to that board and card after the IdP round-trip. After callback the app lands on / (root dashboard) and the original path is discarded.

Post-login routing must restore returnTo from the pre-auth state. The authorize redirect stored returnTo in sessionStorage under a key that the callback page no longer reads after the auth package split.

Users opening notification emails lose context and have to hunt for the card. Restoring returnTo from the signed state parameter (already round-tripped to the IdP) fixed deep links without relying on sessionStorage.
comments: Broken since auth-web 4.2 when sessionStorage key renamed from nimbus.returnTo to nimbus.auth.returnTo on one side only.
Now encoding returnTo in OAuth state; callback decodes and navigates. Verified with /boards/7?card=1204.

issues.summary: Bulk archive leaves orphaned cards visible until the next poll cycle
description: Bulk archive from the list multi-select removes cards from the server and shows a success toast, but the archived cards remain visible on the board until the next poll (default 30s) or a manual refresh.

Optimistic removal should drop those card ids from the board store immediately. The bulk archive mutation updates the list query cache but not the kanban column entity map, so the board keeps rendering orphans that 404 when opened.
Clicking an orphan opens an error empty state. Syncing board cache eviction with the same id list passed to POST /issues/bulk-archive will clear them without waiting for poll.
comments: Happens only on board view; list view updates instantly after bulk archive.

issues.summary: Search result snippets strip HTML entities incorrectly for ampersands
description: Global search snippets that contain HTML entities for ampersands display wrong. A title stored as R&D roadmap becomes R&amp;D roadmap in the snippet, or sometimes R&D with a stripped character depending on the path.

Snippets should decode entities once and show a single ampersand. Double-encoding happens because the search indexer escapes HTML before Elasticsearch, and the snippet highlighter escapes again when building highlight.fragments.
Readers scanning results for partner names with ampersands waste time opening the wrong hits. Decode before highlight, or mark fragments as already safe and skip the second escape.

issues.summary: Editor undo stack collapses multiple keystrokes into a single step after idle
description: Editor undo (Cmd/Ctrl+Z) normally reverses one logical typing burst. After the user pauses longer than the idle merge window (~800ms) and types again, several distinct keystrokes from the new burst are later undone as a single step, so undo removes more text than expected.

Each continuous typing segment after an idle gap should become its own history item. The history plugin resets the merge timer on idle but reuses the same transaction group id when focus never left the doc, so the next characters join the previous closed step.
Writers who undo carefully lose whole words instead of the last character. Generating a new history group id whenever the idle timer fires would restore per-burst undo.
comments: Idle 1s, type alpha, wait 1s, type beta — one undo wipes both words.
prosemirror-history config has newGroupDelay: 800 but our custom plugin also tags transactions with addToHistory and a sticky groupId. Inspecting that path next.

issues.summary: Invoice line items show tax twice when the workspace uses reverse charge
description: For workspaces with reverse charge VAT enabled, invoice PDFs and the Billing → Invoices detail view show tax amount both as a line-item tax column and again as a separate reverse-charge tax row, effectively doubling the tax display (totals remain correct because one row is a display-only annotation).
Reverse charge invoices should show tax as 0 on lines with a single reverse-charge note, not tax twice. Finance partners flagged PDF exports as non-compliant for their records.

Invoice builder applied the standard tax decorator and the reverse-charge decorator without mutual exclusion. Guarding the standard tax column when tax.regime === reverse_charge removed the duplicate.
comments: Sample invoice INV-10482: line tax 42 EUR and reverse charge note 42 EUR; grand total tax still 0 as expected.
Decorator order was standard then reverse_charge; both wrote into displayTax.
Fix in billing-invoice-render; golden PDF for reverse charge workspace updated.

issues.summary: Avatar upload accepts HEIC files but serves a broken placeholder image
description: Profile avatar upload accepts .heic / .heif (file picker and drag-drop), returns 201, and shows a progress complete state. The served avatar URL then returns a 1x1 broken placeholder PNG instead of a converted image.

Either reject HEIC client-side with a clear message, or transcode to JPEG/WebP on upload and serve that. Today we accept the file, store the original bytes, and the image pipeline fails conversion without failing the upload.
Workers log heic decode not available in this runtime then write the placeholder. Users on iPhone cameras think their photo is set until everyone else sees the broken icon.
comments: Accept list includes image/heic from the mobile upload path; sharp build in the image worker was compiled without HEIF support.

issues.summary: Pinned comment markers disappear when the document is reopened in split view
description: Pinned comment markers (gutter icons that jump to a pinned thread) show correctly in single-pane editor. Opening the same document in split view (two panes, same doc id) causes all pinned markers to disappear in both panes until the document is closed and opened again in single view.

Markers should remain bound to document positions independent of pane count. Split view mounts a second EditorView that re-inits plugin state from an empty pin list because the pin plugin keys state by view instance rather than document id.
Reviewers who use split to compare sections lose pin navigation. Sharing pin plugin state across views for the same doc id should keep markers visible.
comments: Only split view is affected; dual-tab single panes are fine.
PinPlugin state is WeakMap keyed by EditorView — second view starts empty and the first view decorations are destroyed on parent re-render.

issues.summary: Dashboard refresh button triggers two identical network requests in Firefox
description: Clicking the dashboard Refresh control in Firefox fires two identical GETs to the same metrics endpoint within a few milliseconds (e.g. two GET /api/v2/dashboard/summary with the same query string). Chrome and Safari fire one.
A single click should produce one network request. Double fetch wastes quota on heavy summary queries and can flicker widgets that reset loading state twice.

Firefox delivers both the click handler and a residual keyup-as-click on the focused button when Space was used earlier to focus it; the handler is not idempotent. Guarding with an in-flight ref or listening only to click with preventDefault on key repeat should make Firefox match other browsers.

issues.summary: Login form submits twice if Enter is pressed while the request is in flight
description: On the login form, submitting with Enter while the first /auth/login request is still in flight sends a second identical POST. Both can succeed and create two session rows, or the second fails with 409 and surfaces a misleading error over the successful login.

While a login attempt is pending, further submits (button or Enter) must be ignored. The button disables on click but the form onSubmit still accepts Enter because disabled is only on the button, not a submitting flag on the form.
Duplicate sessions confuse session management and rate limits. A isSubmitting guard at the form level before calling the auth client fixes the double POST.

issues.summary: Notification email subject line drops non-ASCII characters from the issue title
description: Notification emails whose issue titles include non-ASCII characters (e.g. accented names, CJK, emoji) arrive with those characters missing from the subject line. Body content retains the correct title.

Subject should preserve the same Unicode as the issue title. The mailer builds subjects with an ASCII-only header encoder path that strips bytes outside 0x20-0x7E instead of applying RFC 2047 encoded-words.
Recipients scanning inbox subjects cannot identify issues with localized titles. Switching subject encoding to UTF-8 encoded-word (or letting the ESP handle Unicode subjects) restores the full title.
comments: Example title with accented characters becomes stripped ASCII-ish garbage in Subject; HTML body is fine.

issues.summary: Board filter URL params are lost when opening a card in a new tab
description: When a board is filtered (e.g. assignee=me and status=in_progress in the query string), using Open in new tab on a card preserves only /cards/{id} and drops the filter query string from the opener URL context. That is expected for the card URL, but the parent board tab also rewrites its history to strip filter params when the context menu open fires.
Opening a card in a new tab should not mutate the source board filter URL. The board route listens to a global card:open event and calls setSearchParams with only card, wiping other params.
People lose multi-filter setups after middle-clicking a card and have to re-apply filters. Scope the param write to the new tab navigation target only, not the opener history.

issues.summary: Editor table column resize snaps to zero width on the last column
description: In the editor table UI, dragging the resize handle on the last column snaps that column width to 0px on mouseup if the drag ends within 4px of the table right edge. Other columns resize smoothly.

Last column should clamp to a minimum width (currently 48px for others) like every other column. The last handle max delta is computed against container width minus prior columns, but the clamp runs before subtracting scrollbar width (12-16px), so the allowed width becomes negative and snaps to zero.
Tables with a collapsed last column hide cell content and are hard to recover without undo. Applying the same min-width clamp after scrollbar compensation keeps the last column visible.
comments: Easier to hit on Windows where the overlay scrollbar still reserves space in the content box.

issues.summary: Billing usage meter shows negative remaining seats after a plan downgrade
description: After downgrading a workspace plan (e.g. Business 25 seats to Team 10 seats) while 14 seats are still assigned, the Billing usage meter shows -4 seats remaining instead of 0 remaining and 4 over limit.

Remaining seats should floor at zero with a separate overage indicator when active members exceed the new plan cap. Negative remaining confuses admins into thinking the meter is broken and blocks the correct upgrade CTA copy.

Meter computes plan.seats - members.active without clamping; the downgrade webhook updates plan.seats before seat reclamation finishes. Display should use Math.max(0, plan.seats - members.active) and surface overBy when negative.
comments: Reproduced on staging by downgrading a workspace with 14 members to the 10-seat Team plan; meter read -4 for about six hours until someone removed members.
Billing UI pulls raw seats_remaining from /billing/usage; API will clamp and add seats_overage in the same payload.

issues.summary: Keyboard focus trap on the workspace invite modal cannot be dismissed with Esc
description: The workspace invite modal traps focus for keyboard users as intended, but pressing Escape does not close it. Overlay click and the X button still work.

Escape should dismiss the modal and restore focus to the Invite trigger. The dialog registers a keydown listener on the modal node only; when focus is inside a nested focusable (email input), the event does not bubble to that listener because stopPropagation runs on the input enter-to-add-chip handler for all keys.

Keyboard-only admins cannot bail out without Tabbing to the close control. Moving Escape handling to document while the modal is mounted (and ignoring it when a nested popover is open) restores expected dialog behavior.

issues.summary: Dashboard empty state illustration flashes on every data refetch
description: On dashboards that already have data, each background refetch briefly mounts the empty-state illustration (cloud with No activity yet) for a flash before the loaded data paints again. First load empty state is correct when there is truly no data.

Refetch should keep showing the previous data or a subtle loading affordance, not the empty illustration. The query sets data to undefined while isFetching is true because keepPreviousData / placeholderData is not enabled on the summary query.
The flash is distracting on 15s polling and looks like a reliability bug. Enabling placeholder previous data (or gating empty state on isLoading && !data) removes the flicker.
comments: Most noticeable on slow 3G throttling; empty art pops every poll.

issues.summary: SSO login fails when the IdP returns a NameID with mixed case domain
description: SSO login fails when the IdP assertion NameID email has a mixed-case domain (e.g. User@Example.COM) while the Nimbus user record stores the domain lowercased (user@example.com). Local-part case handling is already fine; only the domain comparison breaks.

Authentication should succeed when the case-insensitive email matches a provisioned user. Today the SSO callback does an exact string match on the full NameID against users.email, returning No user matched this identity for mixed-case domains.

Enterprise IdPs often emit domains in the case registered in their directory. Normalizing both sides with a domain-lowercase (RFC 5321) compare before lookup should allow login without forcing customers to re-provision.
comments: Customer IdP sends NameID as alex.kim@Corp.Example.COM; our user row is alex.kim@corp.example.com. Password login works; SSO does not.
Auth service compare is nameId === user.email. Planning to normalize with email domain rules and add a case-variant fixture.

issues.summary: Editor slash command menu stays open after switching to another browser tab
description: Invoking a slash command in the editor opens the command menu. If the user switches to another browser tab while the menu is open, then returns, the menu is still open and positioned at stale coordinates, often floating over unrelated content until Escape is pressed.

Leaving the document (blur of the window or editor) should close the slash menu like other editor popovers. The slash plugin listens for focusout on the editor root but ignores document.visibilitychange and window blur, so tab switches never dismiss it.
Stale menus capture the next keystrokes when the user returns, inserting a command they no longer want. Closing on visibilitychange hidden and on editor blur aligns with mention and emoji pickers.

issues.summary: Notification digests duplicate events that occurred near the midnight boundary
description: Daily digest emails assembled after 00:00 UTC sometimes list the same card activity twice when the underlying event timestamp sits within a few minutes of the day boundary. A workspace that ran a digest at 00:07 UTC saw three assignment changes from 23:58–00:02 appear once under “Yesterday” and again under “Today”.

Expected behavior is that each event_id contributes to exactly one digest window. The window should close on the exclusive upper bound of the previous calendar day in the workspace timezone, not on the worker’s clock alone.

What we observe is double inclusion whenever the digest job’s dayKey is derived from UTC while event buckets are still keyed with America/Los_Angeles offsets. The likely root cause is that DigestAggregator.hashBucket(workspaceId, dayKey) reuses the UTC day string even after the timezone shift was applied to the query filter, so events near midnight land in two buckets before dedupe runs.
Recipients on plans with digests enabled get noisy mail and start marking Nimbus as spam. Support has three open threads from last week referencing this pattern.
comments: Got another report this morning—digest for workspace w_9182 listed the same comment twice around the Pacific midnight cutover. Whatever we thought was fixed last sprint is still happening on production.

issues.summary: Card labels overflow the chip row without a +N overflow indicator
description: On dense cards that carry more than four labels, the chip row clips the trailing chips against the card edge. There is no “+N” affordance, so reviewers cannot tell how many labels are hidden without opening the card.

Design expects the row to keep visible chips up to the available width, then collapse the remainder into a single overflow chip that shows the count and a tooltip of names. Opening the card should still list every label.

In practice the flex container never measures residual width before paint. Overflow is pure CSS clipping on .label-chip-row, so the count badge never mounts. Hypothesis: LabelChipRow reads maxVisible from a hardcoded 4 instead of computing fit from the card’s content box after the assignee avatar and due-date pill claim space.
Boards with heavy labeling conventions look broken; customers assume labels were deleted.
comments: Reproduced on a card with six labels in the design system board—only three chips show and nothing indicates the rest.
Checking whether size observer on the chip container was dropped in the board virtualization pass last month.
Still broken after the chip spacing tweak shipped yesterday. Overflow count never appears when the fifth label is added; reopening until the measure-fit path is actually wired.

issues.summary: Billing receipt email links open the app root instead of the invoice detail
description: Receipt emails sent after a successful charge include a “View invoice” button and a plain-text URL. Both currently resolve to https://app.example.com/ rather than the invoice detail page for that charge.
Users should land on /billing/invoices/{invoiceId} already authenticated (or prompted to sign in with a return URL). The deep link must survive email client link wrappers.

Actual clicks always hit the app shell home route. The template interpolates {{invoice_url}} from BillingMailer, which was still building paths with only the origin after the billing SPA route rename. Suspect the receipt partial still reads legacy path /account/receipts and the gateway 302s unknown billing paths to /.
Finance contacts cannot jump from mail to the PDF-ready page; ticket volume spiked after the March billing UI redesign.
comments: Confirmed on a Pro monthly charge: button href is bare origin, query string empty.
Root cause was MailLinkBuilder using defaultRoute after InvoiceController moved under /billing. Fixing the path helper and adding a contract test on the rendered HTML.
Staging send with invoice inv_44c1 now opens the detail view; marking done after QA on two major webmail clients.

issues.summary: Dashboard widget drag-and-drop reorders silently fail for the last row
description: Rearranging dashboard widgets works for every row except the bottom-most one. Dragging a widget that currently occupies the last grid row shows the ghost preview, then snaps back to the original index on drop with no toast.
Reorder should persist through PATCH /api/v2/dashboards/{id}/layout and reload with the new order. Failure ought to surface an error if the write is rejected.

Silent no-ops happen only when sourceIndex === layout.length - 1. The client still fires the request, but the payload’s targetIndex is clamped with target capped at length - 2, so the last slot can never receive a move-in. That clamp looks like a leftover guard from when the “add widget” tile occupied a permanent trailing cell.
Power users who keep timeline widgets at the bottom cannot prioritize them without deleting and re-adding the widget.
comments: Layout serializer returns 200 with unchanged positions—matches the clamp theory.
Removed the off-by-one guard and covered last-row up/down moves in DashboardLayout.spec.tsx.
Verified on a six-widget board: bottom chart can move to row 0 and back. Shipping with the dashboard patch.

issues.summary: Password reset token is accepted twice if both tabs submit within 1 second
description: A password-reset link can be consumed twice if two browser tabs both POST the new password within about one second of each other. Both responses return 200 and establish sessions.
Tokens must be single-use: the first successful redemption should invalidate the token atomically so a concurrent attempt receives 410 Gone with “link already used”.

Race is reproducible with two tabs sharing the same token query param. Both hit POST /auth/reset-password before either transaction commits the used_at column. Leading theory is missing SELECT … FOR UPDATE (or an equivalent single-flight Redis lock on token_hash) around the redeem path; the unique partial index on unused tokens is not enough under read-committed isolation.
If a reset email leaks, an attacker and the legitimate user can both set passwords; audit logs show two password_changed events for one token_id.
comments: Load test with 20 parallel redemptions of one token: two succeeded before the lock landed.
Added token redeem advisory lock keyed by sha256(token) and a regression test under concurrent goroutines.
Security review signed off; retested with dual-tab manual flow—second submit now gets 410.

issues.summary: Editor markdown paste converts nested lists into a flat numbered list
description: Pasting markdown that contains nested unordered or ordered lists into the document editor flattens every item into a single top-level numbered list. Nested structure and bullet markers are lost.
Paste of a commonmark-style snippet with two levels of indentation should produce nested list nodes in the editor document tree, preserving ordered vs unordered type per level.

Instead, the HTML clipboard path runs a list normalizer that walks li elements without reading data-indent or nested ul/ol wrappers from the clipboard HTML. Suspected cause: MarkdownPastePlugin converts nested lists to sequential paragraphs first, then ListInputRule renumbers only top-level blocks, discarding depth metadata from the AST.
Writers who draft in external markdown tools spend extra time re-indenting after every paste.

issues.summary: Let users pin a saved view to the sidebar
description: Saved views already live under the board filter menu, but frequent views still take two clicks to reopen. Several design partners asked to pin a view so it appears as a persistent entry under the project sidebar.

Proposal: from the saved-view overflow menu, “Pin to sidebar” stores pin_order on the view record (max 8 pins per user per project). Sidebar shows the pin label; clicking applies the same filter/sort payload as opening the view from the menu. Unpin is available from both sidebar context menu and the view manager.

Acceptance: pinned views survive reload, respect sharing (private pins stay private), and do not appear for users lacking view:read. Reordering pins via drag updates pin_order without changing the underlying query.
comments: Product wants pins to be per-user, not per-workspace—confirming that before we touch the schema.
Sidebar nav mock in the design mock is ready; engineering can start on the pin_order column.

issues.summary: Allow bulk reassignment of cards from the board multi-select toolbar
description: Reassigning many cards today means opening each card or using a brittle CSV round-trip. Ops teams running sprint cleanup need a multi-select path that does not leave the board.

When two or more cards are selected, the multi-select toolbar gains “Reassign…”, opening a member picker. Confirm calls POST /boards/{id}/cards/bulk-reassign with card_ids and assignee_id (or null to unassign). Activity feed records one bulk event plus per-card assignee history.
Done when selection of 50 cards reassigns within 3s on a median board, permissions mirror single-card assign rules, and partial failures return which card_ids were skipped.
comments: Bulk endpoint landed behind a flag; toolbar wiring merged this morning.
Load test at 200 cards hit a gateway timeout—bumped worker batch size to 40 and retried.
Flag default-on in production after support dogfood; closing.

issues.summary: Show estimated vs actual cycle time on the dashboard velocity chart
description: The velocity chart currently plots completed points per sprint only. Planning leads also want estimated cycle time (from the sprint commitment snapshot) drawn against actual median cycle time for finished cards.

Extend the dashboard velocity series with two optional lines: estimate_hours from the sprint planning freeze, and actual_cycle_hours computed as entered_done_at − first_in_progress_at. Toggle in widget settings defaults to on for new widgets, off for existing ones to avoid surprising layout shifts.
Ship criteria: tooltips show both values for a sprint column, empty sprints omit the actual line, and the export CSV gains estimate_cycle_h and actual_cycle_h columns.
comments: Need clarity on whether estimate should use story points conversion or the numeric estimate field—will park until analytics weighs in.

issues.summary: Add a read-only share link for dashboards without requiring a full seat
description: Stakeholders often need to see a dashboard without burning a paid seat. Today the only options are full invites or static screenshots that rot immediately.

Introduce a read-only share link: workspace admins generate a link token with optional expiry (7 / 30 / never) and optional password. GET /public/dashboards/{token} renders widgets without edit chrome, live data refresh every 60s, and no sidebar navigation into the rest of the app.
Acceptance includes revoke, rotate, audit log entry on create/revoke, rate limit of 120 req/min per token, and blocked access when the parent dashboard is deleted.
comments: Token model and public renderer skeleton are up in a draft PR; still wiring password challenge.
Legal asked for a watermark option—adding a non-default “Shared from Nimbus” footer before we call this review-ready.

issues.summary: Let editors insert collapsible callout blocks from the slash menu
description: Writers repeatedly fake callouts with blockquotes and emoji. That breaks consistency and is invisible to our a11y tree as a distinct region.

Add a slash-menu item “Callout” that inserts a collapsible callout block with variants info / warn / success, an optional title, and a chevron that toggles body visibility. Collapsed state is stored on the node attrs and syncs to collaborators.

Ready when slash menu search matches “callout”, “note”, and “warning”; keyboard users can expand/collapse with Enter on the header; export to markdown uses a fenced callout convention we already parse on import.
comments: Schema change for callout attrs is straightforward—will mirror the toggle-list collapse flag.

issues.summary: Surface upcoming invoice amount on the billing settings overview
description: Billing settings show the current plan and payment method but not what the next invoice is expected to charge. Finance owners want that figure without downloading last month’s PDF.

On the billing overview card, surface upcoming_invoice_amount and upcoming_invoice_date from the billing provider preview API, formatted in the workspace currency. Include a breakdown link to line items (seats, metered usage, credits).
Complete when the amount updates within 15 minutes of seat changes, shows “Usage still metering” when the preview is partial, and hides the block for free-tier workspaces.
comments: Preview API latency was ~900ms—cached the response for 10 minutes keyed by workspace and seat revision.
QA signed off on mid-cycle seat add; amount ticked up as expected. Closing the story.

issues.summary: Support keyboard-only navigation through the notification inbox
description: The notification inbox is largely mouse-driven: row focus is inconsistent, and several actions (mark read, archive, open target) are not reachable without a pointer.

Support full keyboard use: arrow keys move roving tabindex across rows, Enter opens the deep link, e archives, r toggles read, and Escape returns focus to the inbox toggle. Screen readers should announce unread count changes via an aria-live region already used by the badge.
Done when automated a11y scan clean on the inbox panel, documented shortcuts in the ? help popover, and a end-to-end path covers a 20-item inbox without mouse APIs.

issues.summary: Allow workspace admins to force SSO for all new member invitations
description: Some regulated workspaces need every new member to authenticate via SSO from the first login. Today invites can still choose password signup if the admin only enabled SSO without enforcing it.

Add a workspace auth setting force_sso_for_invites. When true, invitation emails send users through the IdP only; password and magic-link signup routes reject invite tokens for that workspace with a clear error. Existing password members are unaffected until a separate migration policy is chosen.
Shipped criteria: default off, only owners can toggle, Directory-provisioned users already SSO-bound keep working, and audit log records enforcement changes.
comments: Enforcement flag is live; invite accept flow redirects to /sso/start with workspace_hint.
Customer pilot on two enterprise tenants completed without password bypass. Done.

issues.summary: Let users snooze a notification for 1 hour, tomorrow, or next week
description: Users get interrupted by low-urgency notifications they want to see later, not dismiss forever. Archive is too permanent; leaving them unread keeps the badge noisy.

On each notification row and the desktop toast, offer Snooze with presets: 1 hour, tomorrow 9:00 local, and next Monday 9:00 local. Snoozed items leave the inbox and reappear at the scheduled time as unread with a “Snoozed” provenance chip.
Acceptance: cancel snooze from the scheduled list, respect quiet-hours if that ships later, and cap at 100 concurrent snoozes per user to protect the scheduler.
comments: Scheduler jobs use the existing delayed_jobs queue with notif_snooze_ prefix.
Tweaked “tomorrow” to use the user’s profile timezone instead of UTC after beta feedback.
Metrics show ~12% of active notif users tried snooze in week one; marking complete.

issues.summary: Add a compact density mode for the kanban board on laptop screens
description: Kanban columns feel cramped on 13–14" laptop viewports once cards show cover images and three metadata rows. Horizontal scroll becomes the default interaction.

Introduce a Compact density mode under board view options: reduces card padding, hides cover images, collapses description previews, and tightens column width to 260px. Preference is stored per user per board.

Exit criteria: density toggle is keyboard reachable, print/export still uses comfortable density, and boards with 12+ columns fit a 1440px-wide window without horizontal scroll in compact mode for typical card content.

issues.summary: Show inline diffs when two collaborators edit the same paragraph
description: When two people edit the same paragraph, the last writer often overwrites the other with only a coarse “conflict” toast. Users want to see both versions before choosing.

If presence detects concurrent edits on the same block_id, show an inline diff gutter: remote insertions in one highlight, local in another, with Accept mine / Accept theirs / Merge line-by-line actions. Diffs are character-level for short paragraphs and line-level above 280 characters.
Ready when conflicts no longer auto-apply remote wins, analytics track merge outcomes, and the flow works for at least two simultaneous peers on a single block.
comments: The collab layer already has the dual versions—UI is the missing piece. Spike branch renders a basic split view.

issues.summary: Let billing admins download a usage CSV for any completed billing period
description: Billing admins exporting usage today screenshot the charts or ask support for a manual dump. Finance needs a self-serve CSV for any closed billing period.

On the usage page, “Download CSV” lists closed periods (up to 24 months). Selecting one generates a file with columns: date, meter_name, quantity, unit, workspace_id, project_id. Generation is async for files over ~5MB with an email to the requester at billing@example.com style addresses on the account.
Done when downloads match the numbers on the usage chart within 0.5%, in-progress periods are disabled, and only billing_admin and owner roles see the control.
comments: CSV worker is writing files to object storage; still wiring the signed download URL TTL (15 minutes).
Discovered project_id is null for workspace-level meters—documenting that in the CSV header comment row.

issues.summary: Allow pinning an editor template as the default for new documents
description: Teams standardize on a few document templates but still pick the template manually every time. New docs often start blank and get reformatted later.

From the template gallery, allow “Set as default for new documents” scoped to a project (or workspace if no project context). The new-doc modal preselects that template and can still switch. Defaults are role-aware: editors and above can set project defaults; only admins set workspace defaults.
Acceptance: clearing the default restores the blank doc, API exposes default_template_id on project settings, and mobile new-doc flow honors the same default.
comments: Project settings field is in review; editor bootstrap still hardcodes blank—connecting that next.
Need a migration note for workspaces that already stuffed a template id into an undocumented prefs key.

issues.summary: Add a dashboard widget that lists issues blocked for more than 7 days
description: Blocked work ages quietly on boards. Managers want a dashboard signal when cards sit in a blocked state longer than a week without scanning every column.

New widget “Long-blocked issues” queries cards where blocked=true (or status category blocked) and blocked_since < now() - 7 days. List shows title, board, age in days, and blocker reason if present; click opens the card. Configurable threshold defaulting to 7 with options 3 / 7 / 14.
Ship when empty state explains “No cards blocked beyond threshold”, refresh matches other list widgets (5 min), and the widget respects board-level permissions of the viewer.

issues.summary: Let users configure quiet hours for desktop and mobile push alerts
description: Push alerts fire at all hours. Users want a quiet window for desktop and mobile independently so overnight pings stop without disabling notifications entirely.

Under notification preferences, add Quiet hours with start/end times, timezone (default profile TZ), and channel toggles for desktop push vs mobile push. During the window, pushes are held and delivered as a single summary at window end unless the event is marked critical (security alerts).
Criteria: server-side enforcement so background workers do not bypass the client, preview of next quiet window on the settings page, and an escape hatch “Allow critical” defaulting to on.
comments: Should email digests honor quiet hours too, or only push? Parking email out of scope for v1.

issues.summary: Support importing a board from a CSV with custom field mapping
description: Importing boards from spreadsheets currently forces a fixed column map and drops unknown headers. Customers migrating from other tools need to bind CSV columns to Nimbus fields including custom fields.

Import wizard: upload CSV (max 10k rows), auto-detect headers, then a mapping UI from each column to title, description, status, assignee email, due date, or a custom field key. Unmapped columns can be ignored or attached as labels. Dry-run reports row errors before commit.
Released when sample CSVs for two common board-tool exports are in docs, failed rows download as a residual CSV, and the bulk import worker emits progress on the existing job status channel.
comments: Mapping UI and dry-run validation merged; worker reuses the bulk card create path.
Customer import of 4.2k rows completed with 17 row errors in the residual file—acceptable. Closing.

issues.summary: Show password strength and common-breach checks on the signup form
description: Signup only checks minimum length today. Weak and previously breached passwords still get accepted until a later forced reset.

On the signup password field, show a strength meter (entropy-style score 0–4) and an async check against our common-breach bloom filter service. Block submit on score < 2 or a breach hit; show actionable guidance without listing the password in logs.
Done when the check debounces at 300ms, fails open with a warning if the breach service times out after 800ms, and the same component is reused on password change.
comments: Breach service client shipped with a 50ms local cache for repeated prefixes.
UX copy review passed; enabling on production signup.

issues.summary: Allow filtering the notification feed by project and event type
description: The notification feed mixes every project and event type into one stream. People watching a single launch project cannot isolate signal from noise.

Add filter chips and a filter panel: multi-select projects the user belongs to, and event types (assignment, mention, status change, due soon, billing). Filters persist in local storage per user and apply to both inbox and the full feed page. Unread badge counts remain global unless “count only filtered” is toggled later—out of scope here.
Complete when deep links preserve filter query params, empty states explain active filters, and API GET /notifications accepts project_ids[] and types[] with a 100-item page size.
comments: API filters landed first; UI chips followed in the same release train.
Minor bug with “select all projects” cleared in a patch; story is done.

issues.summary: Let power users define reusable dashboard layouts shared with the team
description: Individuals rearrange dashboards carefully, then teammates rebuild the same layout by hand. Teams want a shared layout object they can apply without copying widget JSON.

Allow power users (dashboard:admin) to save the current layout as a named reusable layout, optionally share it with the workspace. Others can “Apply layout” which clones widget config and queries but not live filter personalization. Version field increments on overwrite.
Acceptance: max 25 shared layouts per workspace, apply is undoable for 30s, and personal drafts stay private until shared.
comments: Schema for dashboard_layouts is up; applying a layout currently resets date range filters—discussing whether to preserve them.
Sharing ACLs mirror dashboard visibility; writing tests for guest role denial.

issues.summary: Add an accessibility audit checklist panel for published documents
description: Published docs go out without a consistent accessibility pass. Authors ask for an in-product checklist instead of an external spreadsheet.

Add a side panel “Accessibility audit” on published (and publish-preview) documents: automated checks for missing alt text, heading order gaps, low-contrast text tokens we control, and link text like “click here”. Each item is pass/fail with jump-to-node. Manual checklist items (keyboard walkthrough, screen reader spot check) can be ticked by the author and stored on the publish record.
Shipped when publish is not hard-blocked by fails (warn only), the panel is keyboard accessible, and results appear in the publish history snapshot.
comments: Automated rules reuse the editor’s a11y visitor from the callout work.
Docs team ran the checklist on five help articles; closing as complete.

issues.summary: Surface trial days remaining as a non-blocking banner for workspace owners
description: Trial end currently surprises owners at conversion or via a single email. Owners want a calm, persistent reminder of days left without modal interruption.

Show a non-blocking banner for workspace owners (and billing admins) when trial_ends_at is within the trial window: “N days left in your trial” with links to compare plans and manage billing. Dismiss lasts 24 hours; banner returns until conversion or expiry. At 3 days and 1 day, emphasize urgency with stronger but still non-modal styling.
Done when the banner never appears for converted workspaces, respects role checks, and is hidden inside public share views.
comments: Banner component wired to /billing/trial-status; still need the 24h dismiss key in user prefs.
Copy review prefers “trial ends on {date}” over only day counts—updating strings.

issues.summary: Let users mirror a single list column into another workspace as read-only
description: Cross-workspace visibility today requires dual membership and manual sync. Some programs need a single list column visible elsewhere without granting write access.

From a list column menu, “Mirror to workspace…” creates a read-only mirrored column in a target workspace the actor admins. Card titles, status, and assignees replicate one-way within 2 minutes; edits in the source propagate, edits in the mirror are rejected. Break-mirror is available on either side with confirmation.
Released when audit logs record mirror create/break, attachments are metadata-only (no binary clone) in v1, and cycle detection blocks A→B→A setups.
comments: Replication uses the outbox pattern on card updates; lag p99 ~45s in staging.
Support runbook added; feature flag removed after two weeks stable.

issues.summary: Allow attaching a payment method without immediately changing the plan
description: Storing a payment method today still routes through the change-plan checkout sheet, which scares teams who only want a backup instrument on file before renewal.

Split the flow: “Add payment method” stores the instrument via the billing provider setup intent without changing plan_id or triggering proration. Plan changes stay on a separate “Change plan” path that can reuse the default method.

Acceptance: users with a method and no plan change see no invoice preview; failed setup intents do not leave orphan customer objects; the settings page shows methods with a default star independent of plan tier.
comments: Checkout sheet was tightly coupled to plan_id—extracting setup-intent-only mode now.
Provider test-mode path works; exercising the sandbox processor next.

issues.summary: Add slash-command shortcuts for inserting date chips with relative offsets
description: Inserting dates in docs requires the date picker or typing a full ISO string. Writers want relative shortcuts while outlining schedules.

Slash commands: /date, /today, /tomorrow, /+3d, /-1w insert date chips with the resolved calendar day stored in UTC midnight of the workspace TZ, displayed in the viewer’s locale. Chips remain updateable via the existing date popover.
Complete when invalid offsets show inline errors, commands appear in the slash palette with examples, and collaborative peers see the same absolute day.
comments: Parser covers d/w/m suffixes; months use calendar add not fixed 30-day math.
Shipped in editor 3.12; docs snippet published on example.com/help/date-chips.

issues.summary: Let admins require MFA for any role at or above editor
description: Workspace MFA can be optional today even for roles that can edit production content. Admins in stricter environments need to require MFA for editor and any higher privilege role.

Auth policy setting: minimum_mfa_role = editor | admin | owner | off. Members at or above that role who lack a verified second factor are put into a soft-gate on next session: they can only reach MFA enrollment until complete. API tokens minted before enrollment keep working until expiry but cannot create new long-lived tokens.
Backlog-ready acceptance sketch: grace period option of 0 or 7 days, owner cannot lock themselves out without a recovery code path, and directory-synced users follow the same gate.

issues.summary: Show a changelog drawer for document versions without leaving the editor
description: Version history currently navigates authors away from the editing surface into a separate history route, breaking flow during reviews.

Add a changelog drawer anchored to the editor chrome listing versions with actor, timestamp, and optional message. Selecting a version shows a read-only preview beside the live doc; restore remains a two-click confirm. Drawer can stay open while the user continues editing the live version.
Success metrics: opening history no longer unmounts the editor session, keyboard Esc closes the drawer, and large docs (500+ versions) virtualize the list.
comments: Curious whether comments on old versions belong in this drawer or stay out of v1—leaning out.

issues.summary: Allow muting notifications for a specific card until it is reassigned
description: Watching a noisy card floods the inbox when the user only cares after ownership moves. Muting the whole board is too broad; unwatching loses future reassignment signals they do want.

Per-card control: “Mute until reassigned” suppresses notifications for that card_id for the current user until assignee_id changes, then automatically clears the mute and delivers a single reassignment notification. Manual unmute is always available on the card and in notification settings under Active mutes.
Acceptance: mutes sync across devices, do not affect other watchers, and expire after 90 days of no reassignment with an optional reminder.

issues.summary: Add integration tests for the bulk import worker
description: The bulk import worker has grown edge cases (custom field mapping, partial row failure, assignee email resolution) but still relies on manual staging runs. Regressions slip into release candidates.

Done when we have an integration suite under workers/import that spins the worker against a test database and fixture CSVs: happy path 100 rows, malformed custom field, unknown assignee skip, 10k-row performance budget under 60s wall time in CI, and poison-message retry. Suite runs in CI on workers package changes.

issues.summary: Migrate dashboard chart tooltips to the shared floating-ui primitives
description: Dashboard chart tooltips still mount a one-off positioning helper that diverges from the shared floating primitives used by the rest of the app. Arrow placement and collision behavior disagree with design system defaults, and the helper breaks under strict mode double-mount.

Complete when all chart tooltip surfaces (velocity, burndown, distribution, usage) use the shared portal plus offset middleware, visual regression screenshots update, and the legacy tooltip position utility is deleted from the dashboard package with no remaining imports.
comments: Velocity and burndown migrated; distribution still uses the old anchor math for stacked segments.
Shift middleware fixed the clipped tooltip on the rightmost bar—continuing with usage chart next.

issues.summary: Document the editor collaborative protocol handshake for SDK consumers
description: SDK partners keep filing support tickets because the collab handshake sequence lives only in a private design doc from Q3 2024. Without a public reference, integrators reverse-engineer the wire format from packet captures and ship clients that break when we rotate the protocol minor version.

Publish a dedicated section under docs/sdk/collab covering the three-phase handshake: HELLO with clientCapabilities, READY with serverEpoch and presenceLeaseMs, then the first presence snapshot. Include the exact JSON shapes for each frame type and the 2.1-second timeout before the gateway tears down an incomplete session.

Done when the page is linked from the SDK README, includes at least one annotated sequence diagram, and a sample Node snippet that completes the handshake against wss://collab.example.com/v1. Review sign-off from Editor platform and DevRel.
comments: Draft lives in docs/sdk/collab/handshake.md; sequence diagram uses the mermaid source from the design doc so we do not drift again.
DevRel requested a second example that shows resuming after a network blip — added the RESUME frame under the recovery subsection.
Merged and published to the public docs site. Support will point the next collab SDK ticket at this page.

issues.summary: Extract billing proration helpers into a shared package with unit coverage
description: Proration math is duplicated in billing-service, the invoice worker, and the admin CLI. Three implementations already disagree on mid-cycle seat changes: the service rounds half-up after tax, the worker rounds before tax, and the CLI skips partial-day credits entirely.

Move calculateSeatProration, applyCreditBalance, and buildProrationLineItems into @nimbus/billing-proration with a pure unit suite covering 0-day, single-day, leap-day, and multi-currency inputs. Call sites import the package and delete their local copies.

issues.summary: Replace legacy localStorage auth tokens with the httpOnly session cookie path
description: Auth tokens still land in localStorage under nimbus.session.v1. Any XSS on a marketing subdomain can steal long-lived bearer strings and call the Graph API as the victim until the 14-day TTL expires.

Switch the web app to the httpOnly session cookie path already used by the mobile BFF: Set-Cookie with Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, and a 12-hour sliding max-age. Drop the Authorization header injection from the SPA bootstrap and rely on credentials: include for same-site calls.
Complete when localStorage no longer holds session material, CSRF double-submit is wired for mutating POSTs, and the auth smoke suite passes on Chrome and Safari.
comments: Security review flagged that the marketing subdomain still shares the parent cookie domain — need to scope the cookie to app.example.com before flip.
Staging flag auth_httponly_cookie is on for internal accounts; plan to expand to 5% of production traffic next week.

issues.summary: Add Storybook stories for notification toast variants and stacking rules
description: Notification toasts have four visual variants and a stacking policy that only exists as tribal knowledge in the Notifications channel. Design reviews keep regressing spacing when engineers guess the rules.

Add Storybook stories for success, warning, error, and info toasts, plus a multi-toast canvas that exercises the 3-toast max stack, 280ms enter/exit, and bottom-right collision with the help FAB. Document the z-index band 1200–1290 in the story description.
Acceptance: stories render under Chromatic, stacking story matches the Figma density spec within 2px, and the Notifications README links to the Storybook path.
comments: Chromatic project is ready; need the stories package name confirmed with design-system before landing.

issues.summary: Wire axe accessibility checks into the Dashboard CI smoke suite
description: Dashboard CI only runs unit and visual snapshot jobs. Accessibility regressions — missing labels on the filter drawer, contrast failures on the density toggle — ship unnoticed until a customer files a ticket.

Wire axe-core into the existing Playwright smoke suite for the four primary Dashboard routes: /board, /timeline, /reports, and /settings/workspace. Fail the job on any serious or critical violation; log moderate findings without blocking.
Done when the smoke workflow posts an axe summary artifact and at least one intentional a11y failure is proven to red the pipeline in a dry-run PR.
comments: Prefer @axe-core/playwright over the webpack plugin so we reuse the same browser context as the smoke tests.

issues.summary: Refactor workspace scope middleware to accept multi-tenant request contexts
description: Workspace scope middleware assumed a single tenantId per request, pulled from the JWT claim alone. Multi-tenant service accounts that act across several workspaces in one call hit 403s because the middleware overwrote the ambient scope on the first membership check.

Refactor resolveWorkspaceScope to accept an optional RequestContext with tenantIds[], actorType, and impersonationFlag. Membership resolution unions the allowed set rather than short-circuiting on the first match. Keep the single-tenant path as a thin wrapper so existing handlers stay untouched.
Complete when integration tests cover three tenants in one request, the impersonation audit log still records each workspace id, and p95 latency on the middleware stays under 4ms on staging.
comments: First cut still mutated a shared AsyncLocalStorage bag — switched to a frozen context object per request.
Load test on staging with 50 concurrent multi-tenant calls looks clean; no 403 spikes.
Shipped in release 2025.11.3. Closing.

issues.summary: Remove the deprecated filter chip color tokens from the design system
description: Filter chip color tokens --chip-filter-bg-legacy and --chip-filter-fg-muted-v1 still ship in the design-system CSS bundle even though no product surface imports them after the 2025 palette refresh. They inflate the token dump and confuse designers scanning the Figma-to-code map.

Delete the deprecated token definitions, remove them from the theme export map, and bump the design-system minor so consumers that still reference them get a clear compile break rather than silent fallbacks.
comments: Grep across monorepo shows zero remaining usages outside the token file itself — safe to delete.

issues.summary: Add performance budgets for the editor initial paint on mid-tier laptops
description: Editor first paint on mid-tier laptops (Intel i5-1135G7 class, 16GB RAM) regularly exceeds 3.2s LCP in field data, yet we have no CI gate that fails when a PR worsens that path. Mobile budgets exist; desktop editor is unchecked.

Add a Lighthouse CI budget job targeting the editor route with CPU 4x throttle and 4G Fast profile. Cap initial paint at 2.4s, TBT at 350ms, and total JS transferred at 420 KiB for the editor chunk graph.
Complete when the budget file lives in tooling/perf/editor-budget.json, the job runs on every editor-package PR, and the baseline commit is recorded in the perf dashboard.
comments: Baseline captured on a macbook-air-m1 with forced CPU throttle to approximate the i5 profile — numbers match RUM p75 within 8%.
First PR that added an unlazy-loaded emoji picker correctly failed the budget; good signal.
Budget is live on main. Handing off ownership to Editor platform.

issues.summary: Generate OpenAPI types for the billing portal session create endpoint
description: The billing portal session create endpoint (POST /v1/billing/portal-sessions) has an OpenAPI path but clients still hand-write request and response types. Drift between the YAML and TypeScript caused two production 400s last quarter when returnUrl became required.

Generate TypeScript types from the OpenAPI document into packages/billing-api-types using openapi-typescript, export CreatePortalSessionRequest and CreatePortalSessionResponse, and wire the portal client to consume them. Add a CI check that fails if the generated file is stale relative to the YAML.
Done when the generator runs in the billing package build, consumers import from @nimbus/billing-api-types, and the stale-check job is green on main.
comments: openapi-typescript 7.x required a small patch for the oneOf on BillingPortalMode — documented in the package README.
CI stale check caught a missed YAML change on the first try. Merged.

issues.summary: Backfill missing notification preference rows for workspaces created before 2025
description: Workspaces created before 2025-01-01 never received rows in notification_preferences. Those accounts fall through to hard-coded defaults in the notification service, so product changes to default digests never reach them and support cannot toggle channels per workspace.

Backfill one preference row per (workspace_id, channel) for email, in_app, and slack with digest_frequency=weekly and quiet_hours_enabled=false. Run in batches of 2_500 workspaces with a 150ms pause to keep write IOPS under the RDS alert threshold. Idempotent on workspace_id+channel unique key.
comments: Dry-run count: 18_642 workspaces missing at least one channel row. Starting with email only tonight.
Email channel complete for 12k workspaces; in_app batch scheduled for the off-peak window.
Seeing brief lock waits on notification_preferences when the preference UI writes concurrently — lowered batch size to 1_000.

issues.summary: Split the dashboard data loader into parallel queries with a shared cache key
description: The dashboard data loader issued sequential queries for boards, members, and activity, totaling ~640ms p95 on warm cache. That waterfall blocked first contentful paint for the board shell even when each individual query was cheap.

Split loadDashboardBootstrap into three parallel queries sharing a composite cache key workspace:{id}:dash:v3 with a 45-second TTL. Member and activity slices may stale-serve while boards always revalidate on focus.
Complete when the bootstrap path is under 280ms p95 on staging with the shared key, and cache invalidation still fires on board create/archive events.
comments: Initial shared key omitted the membership revision and served a deleted board for one internal user — fixed by adding memRev to the key suffix.
Staging p95 is 251ms after the parallel split. Shipping with the feature flag default on.

issues.summary: Add Playwright coverage for OAuth callback deep-link restoration
description: OAuth callback deep-link restoration has no automated coverage. Manual checks miss the case where the pre-login path includes a query string and hash, so users land on /home instead of the board they were invited to.

Add Playwright specs that start at /oauth/start?return_to= encoded board URLs, complete the mock IdP flow, and assert the final location restores path, search, and hash. Cover both the happy path and an expired state parameter that must bounce to login with an error banner.

issues.summary: Upgrade the markdown sanitizer and update snapshot tests for callout blocks
description: The markdown sanitizer is two major versions behind and strips the new callout block syntax that the editor has emitted since 2025.08. Pasted callouts render as plain paragraphs, and snapshot tests still assert the old stripped output.

Upgrade sanitize-md to 4.6.x, enable the callout extension with allowed types note|warning|tip|danger, and regenerate editor snapshot fixtures for fixtures/callouts/*.md. Confirm script and iframe tags remain stripped under the new defaults.
Done when all editor package snapshots pass, the upgrade note is in the changelog, and a security smoke confirms no new tag allowlist expansion beyond callouts.
comments: 4.6.2 fixed the nested list-inside-callout crash we hit on the first upgrade attempt.
Snapshots updated; security smoke clean. Merged to main.

issues.summary: Instrument billing webhook handlers with structured latency histograms
description: Billing webhook handlers only emit counter metrics for success/failure. When payment events pile up, we cannot tell whether latency lives in signature verification, payload parse, or the ledger write — paging on error rate alone is too late.

Instrument each handler stage with structured histograms: billing.webhook.verify_ms, billing.webhook.parse_ms, and billing.webhook.persist_ms, labeled by event_type and outcome. Export via the existing OTel pipeline with 50/90/99 quantiles.
Acceptance: dashboards show the three stages for invoice.paid and customer.subscription.updated, and an alert fires when p99 of persist_ms exceeds 800ms for 5 minutes.
comments: Need to confirm histogram bucket bounds with observability — current default may crush the sub-10ms verify stage.

issues.summary: Delete unused CSS modules from the pre-2025 editor shell
description: The pre-2025 editor shell left behind 14 CSS modules under packages/editor/src/shell-legacy that no component imports. They still get swept into Storybook's CSS graph and confuse new hires scanning the tree.
Delete the unused modules, remove any orphan className string references in dead test helpers, and confirm the editor production bundle size drops by the measured ~11 KiB gzip.
comments: Confirmed zero import graph edges with madge before scheduling the delete.

issues.summary: Add a feature flag gate for the compact board density experiment
description: The compact board density experiment needs a server-evaluated flag so we can ramp 0→50% of workspaces without a client deploy. Hard-coding the density class in the board shell blocks controlled rollout and clean kill-switch.

Add feature flag board_density_compact via the existing flag service, evaluate it in the dashboard bootstrap payload as density: 'compact' | 'comfortable', and gate the CSS density data-attribute on that value. Default off for all workspaces.
