Complete when flag admin can target by workspace id and plan tier, client respects the bootstrap field without a local override, and kill-switch to off restores comfortable density within one refresh.
comments: Flag registered in staging; bootstrap field wired. Ready for experiment design to set the 10% cohort.

issues.summary: Document keyboard shortcuts in the in-app help drawer data source
description: Keyboard shortcuts for the editor only appear in an external PDF that support links out of product. In-app help drawer lists empty under the Shortcuts section because the data source never received the editor bindings.

Extend help-drawer/shortcuts.json with the editor set: Cmd/Ctrl+B/I/U, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+C for code block, Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+M for comment, and / for the slash menu. Platform-specific labels must resolve from the user agent so Mac and Windows strings stay correct.
Done when the help drawer Shortcuts tab shows the editor group, search finds 'code block', and a unit test freezes the JSON shape against schema version 3.
comments: Product asked to omit the experimental AI shortcut until that flag is GA — left it out of this pass.
Shipped. Support can close the 'where are editor shortcuts' macros.

issues.summary: Normalize timezone conversion helpers used by dashboard date ranges
description: Dashboard date range pickers call three different timezone helpers: one in reports, one in activity, and a copy-pasted function in the board filter bar. They disagree on DST boundaries, so a 'last 7 days' range can shift by an hour depending on which widget you open.

Consolidate on toWorkspaceRange(start, end, workspaceTz) in @nimbus/time, delete the local helpers, and make every dashboard date control go through that API. Unit coverage must include America/Santiago spring-forward and Europe/Paris fall-back for March/October 2025.
comments: Found a fourth helper in the CSV export path — folding that in too so export matches the on-screen range.
Santiago edge case still off by one hour when start is exactly 00:00 local; digging into luxon zone conversion order.
Root cause was converting to UTC before applying workspace zone. Flipping the order; re-running the suite.

issues.summary: Add contract tests between the editor presence channel and the gateway
description: Editor presence frames and the collab gateway have drifted twice this year — once on the peer color field rename, once when leaseMs became required. Manual QA caught both late.

Add contract tests that load the presence protobuf/JSON schema from the gateway repo as a git submodule pin, generate fixtures, and assert the editor client encoder/decoder round-trips PresenceJoin, PresenceCursor, and PresenceLeave without dropping fields.
Complete when CI fails if the submodule pin advances with a breaking schema change the client has not adapted, and the suite runs under packages/editor-presence in under 8 seconds.
comments: Submodule pin set to gateway@3.14.1. First breaking change drill correctly failed CI.
Docs for bumping the pin are in packages/editor-presence/README. Closing.

issues.summary: Migrate notification email templates to the shared MJML layout
description: Notification emails still use per-template HTML with inconsistent header/footer markup. Brand updates require touching 11 files, and three templates still miss the unsubscribe footer required by our ESP policy.

Migrate all notification email templates to the shared MJML layout (layouts/base.mjml) with slots for preheader, body, and footer. Convert issue_assigned, mention, digest_weekly, and export_ready first; remaining seven follow in the same PR if diff stays reviewable.
Done when every template renders through the MJML pipeline, litmus previews match design within the approved tolerance, and the ESP link-scan for unsubscribe succeeds on all of them.
comments: digest_weekly had custom column markup that needed a mj-section rewrite — visual QA signed off.
All 11 templates on the shared layout. ESP scan green. Done.

issues.summary: Cursor pagination skips records when the sort column has duplicate values
description: List endpoints that page with a single-column cursor skip rows when the sort column contains ties. On GET /v2/issues?orderBy=updatedAt&cursor=..., any issues sharing the same updatedAt as the cursor boundary vanish from subsequent pages.

Expected: every issue appears exactly once across the full page walk, with stable ordering for ties. Actual: the opaque cursor stores only updatedAt, so the comparison updatedAt > :cursor drops siblings that share that timestamp. A workspace with 40 issues updated in the same millisecond lost 6 of them between page 1 and page 2.

Likely cause is the cursor codec encoding a single scalar instead of a composite (updatedAt, id) key. Seek predicates need updatedAt > :ts OR (updatedAt = :ts AND id > :id) with id as the tie-breaker.
Integrations that sync the full issue set under-report totals and miss updates. Affects any list route using the shared cursor helper — issues, comments, and projects.
comments: Confirmed on staging with a fixture that forces 25 rows to the same updatedAt; page size 10 dropped 5 rows.
Composite cursor implemented; codec version bumped to v2 so old cursors still decode for one release.
Contract tests added for duplicate sort values. Verified full walk returns 40/40. Shipping.

issues.summary: Webhook delivery retries exhaust the DLQ without surfacing a final failure event
description: When webhook delivery exhausts its retry budget, the worker parks the message on the DLQ and stops. Subscribers never receive a terminal failure event, so their ops dashboards stay green while deliveries are dead.

After the 8th attempt (or the 24-hour retry ceiling), the delivery pipeline should emit webhook.delivery_failed to the subscription's endpoint with the last status code, attempt count, and nextAction=manual_retry. Instead the DLQ write is silent aside from an internal metric.
Hypothesis: the failure publisher is only invoked from the synchronous reject path, not from the DLQ admission hook. The async retry chain marks the job terminal without calling emitTerminalFailure.
Customers monitoring only their own endpoint miss that Nimbus has given up, and support has no customer-visible trail when asked why events stopped.
comments: Reproduced with a subscriber that always returns 503; after attempt 8 the DLQ depth rose and zero delivery_failed events left the gateway.
Hooked emitTerminalFailure into the DLQ admission path and added an idempotency key so double admission cannot double-notify.
Load test with 500 doomed deliveries: 500 terminal events, no extras. Deployed to production.

issues.summary: Rate limiter window resets early under clock skew between API nodes
description: API rate limiter windows reset earlier than the configured 60-second bucket when nodes disagree on wall-clock time. Clients suddenly get a full quota again mid-window, then slam into 429s when traffic lands on a node with a correct clock.

Expected behavior is a fixed window anchored to a shared time source so remaining quota decreases monotonically within the window. Observed: under ~180ms skew between api-node-3 and the Redis-backed counter host, local windowStart calculations fall into the prior bucket and refill prematurely.
Root hypothesis: each node computes windowStart = floor(localNow / 60s) instead of using Redis TIME or a logical bucket id from the store. Clock skew directly shifts the bucket index.
Bursty clients appear to break through limits, then trigger false-positive abuse alerts on the next correctly timed node hop.
comments: ntp drift on api-node-3 was 220ms at incident time — matches the repro window.
Switched bucket indexing to Redis TIME-based IDs; local clocks no longer influence the window.
Chaos test injecting ±500ms skew no longer refills early. Closed.

issues.summary: SDK listIssues ignores the expand=changelog query parameter on v2.4 clients
description: SDK listIssues on the v2.4 client line silently drops expand=changelog. Callers pass the parameter, the HTTP layer builds the query string, but the typed client strips unknown expand tokens before send.

Expected: changelog histories return in the expand payload when requested. Actual: the request leaves the SDK without expand, so responses never include histories and apps fall back to N+1 getIssue calls.
Likely an allowlist in ExpandParams for v2.4 that never added changelog after the server enabled it in API 2.3. v2.5 clients are fine; only the frozen 2.4 line is affected.
Partner integrations pinned to 2.4 show empty activity panels and extra rate-limit pressure from compensatory fetches.
comments: Need to confirm whether we patch 2.4.x or only document the upgrade — checking support volume.

issues.summary: Worker crashes when the job payload contains nested null optional fields
description: Export and reindex workers crash hard when a job payload includes nested optional fields explicitly set to null. The panic is a null pointer during struct decode, not a handled validation error.

Payloads with nested null optionals should either coerce to omitted or reject with a permanent failure reason. Instead the worker process exits, the job returns to the queue, and the crash loop burns the pod restart budget.

Hypothesis: the generated payload structs use nested value types rather than pointers/Option, so unmarshalling cannot represent null and aborts. Top-level nulls are fine; only nested optionals trip it.
Long-running export queues stall whenever a client omits a filter by sending null instead of leaving the key out.
comments: Stack trace points at decodeFilter.Assignee in worker-common — matches nested null.
Changed nested optionals to pointer fields and added a fuzz fixture of null-heavy payloads.
No crashes in 12h soak on staging with the null fuzzer. Deployed.

issues.summary: REST API returns 500 instead of 422 for invalid ISO-8601 due dates
description: POST /v2/issues and PATCH due-date paths return HTTP 500 when the due date string fails ISO-8601 parsing. Clients treat 500 as a platform outage and retry, amplifying load.

Invalid values like 2025-13-40 or 2025-04-31T25:00:00Z should yield 422 with a field error on dueDate. Actual response is an unhandled time.Parse panic recovered as a generic 500 with request id only.

Cause hypothesis: parseDueDate sits behind the service layer after auth and rate limiting, and its error is not mapped through the validation error type that the HTTP layer turns into 422. Only the happy-path time.Time conversion is tested.
SDK users and third-party integrators surface noisy outage alerts for what is simply bad input.
comments: Added a table-driven test of 12 invalid due date strings; all were 500 before the fix.
Mapped parse errors to FieldViolation{field: dueDate}. Contract tests assert 422.
Production error rate for this path dropped to zero after deploy. Closing.

issues.summary: Webhook signature header uses the previous secret for 30 seconds after rotation
description: After a webhook secret rotation, the X-Nimbus-Signature header continues to use the previous secret for roughly 30 seconds. Receivers that swapped to the new secret immediately reject those deliveries as invalid.

Expected: once rotation commits, new deliveries sign with the new secret; dual-sign (both secrets) may cover a short grace window if documented. Actual: a cache on the signing path keeps the old secret until its 30-second TTL expires, with no dual-sign.

Hypothesis: secret material is cached in the delivery worker with key sub:{id}:signing without a publish-time invalidation. Rotation updates Postgres but not the cache, so the worker keeps HMAC-ing with the stale value until TTL.
Security-conscious customers who rotate after a leak see a burst of signature failures and may disable the subscription.
comments: Cache dump on a delivery pod still showed the old secret 18s after rotation API returned 200.
Trying explicit cache delete on rotation commit before considering dual-sign grace.
Delete path works in staging; writing the dual-sign option as a follow-up so clients can opt into overlap.

issues.summary: Rate limit headers omit Retry-After on 429 responses from the edge layer
description: When the edge layer returns 429, response headers include X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining but omit Retry-After. Clients that rely on Retry-After for backoff fall back to blind exponential retries and worsen thundering herds.

Expected: 429 responses carry Retry-After as integer seconds until window reset, consistent with the origin API. Actual: only origin-built 429s include it; the edge enforcer synthesizes 429s without copying the reset delta.

Likely gap: the edge template for quota denial sets limit/remaining from the redis counter but never computes resetAt - now for Retry-After. Origin and edge header maps diverged when edge rate limiting shipped.
Official SDKs already honor Retry-After; without it they retry as early as 200ms and trip secondary limits.
comments: Compared edge vs origin header dumps on the same throttled token — Retry-After only on origin.
Edge template now emits Retry-After from the bucket reset timestamp.
SDK integration test against edge staging passes. Done.

issues.summary: SDK webhook verifier fails for payloads larger than 256 KiB
description: The SDK webhook verifier throws or returns invalid signature for bodies larger than 256 KiB even when the HMAC is correct. Large issue.updated payloads with big description fields fail verification every time.

Expected: any body within the platform's 1 MiB webhook cap verifies if the signature matches. Actual: the verifier reads the stream into a 256 KiB buffer and either truncates or errors before computing the digest, so the signature never matches the full body.

Hypothesis: a hard-coded maxBodyVerify = 256 << 10 in the SDK verifier predates the platform raising the webhook body limit to 1 MiB. Server-side signing uses the full body; client-side checks a prefix.
Customers with rich-text heavy projects cannot validate webhooks without a custom verifier.
comments: Reproduced with a 300 KiB fixture body and a known test secret — server sig valid, SDK reports mismatch.
Bumping the buffer to 1 MiB and adding a clear error if Content-Length exceeds the cap.

issues.summary: Bulk update endpoint accepts mixed project keys and partially commits changes
description: POST /v2/issues/bulk-update accepts a batch whose issue keys span multiple projects and applies updates to the subset the caller can write, committing partial success without an error envelope. Callers believe the whole batch applied.

Expected: either reject the batch with 400 when project keys mix under a single-project token, or return a per-item result set with committed/failed flags. Actual: the handler filters unauthorized or cross-project items silently and returns 200 with only the committed ids in the response body, omitting failures.
Hypothesis: authorization is applied per item after the transaction starts, and failed items are skipped without accumulating a failure list. The outer transaction still commits successful rows.
Automation scripts that move status across a program of projects end up with half-applied migrations and no signal to retry the rest.
comments: Wrote a fixture batch of 10 issues across 2 projects; response listed 6 ids and HTTP 200.
Now reject mixed project keys with 400 when the bulk mode is atomic (default), and offer mode=best_effort with explicit per-item errors.
Contract tests cover both modes. Deployed; changelog notes the default atomic behavior.

issues.summary: Worker heartbeat expires while a long-running export holds the same lease
description: Long-running export jobs hold a worker lease that is also used for heartbeats. When export CPU work blocks the event loop past the 30-second heartbeat interval, the lease expires and another worker picks up the same job.

Expected: heartbeat continues for the lifetime of the lease holder, independent of export progress, or export work yields often enough to pump heartbeats. Actual: a single synchronous export of a 2M-row workspace blocks for ~90s; the coordinator expires the lease at 30s and redelivers; two workers write partial export files.

Hypothesis: heartbeat ticks run on the same goroutine/event loop as DoExport and never fire while the CPU-heavy encode loop runs. Separate heartbeat thread or lease extension checkpoints inside the encode loop are missing.
Duplicate exports waste storage and occasionally upload truncated CSVs to the customer bucket.
comments: Traced lease expiry at t=30s while export still on chunk 2 of 7.
Moved heartbeats to a background ticker and added lease extend every 10k rows inside the encode loop.
2M-row export on staging held a single lease for 4m12s with no redelivery. Shipped.

issues.summary: REST search returns stale results for 45 seconds after an issue is reassigned
description: REST search continues to return the previous assignee for ~45 seconds after an issue is reassigned. Filters on the new assignee miss the issue; filters on the old one still hit it.

Expected: search reflects reassignment by the time the update API returns 200, or within the documented near-real-time window of a few seconds. Actual: the search index document keeps the stale assignee until a 45-second refresh cycle, and the update path does not trigger an eager reindex.

Hypothesis: issue update publishes to the search indexer over a debounced queue with maxWaitMs=45000, and assignee-only patches are classified as low priority so they always wait for maxWait rather than flushing early.
Agents sorting queues by assignee see ghost work and miss newly assigned tickets during that window.
comments: Confirmed debounce classification: assignee field is in the deferred set in indexer config.
Moving assignee (and status) to the eager set; measuring indexer load before full rollout.
Staging shows reassignment visible in search within 2s. Watching production lag metrics next.

issues.summary: Webhook subscription list endpoint ignores the pageSize parameter above 50
description: GET /v2/webhook-subscriptions ignores pageSize when the value is above 50. Clients requesting pageSize=100 still receive at most 50 items with no indication the parameter was clamped.

Expected: either honor pageSize up to the documented max of 100, or return 400 when out of range. Actual: the handler silently min(pageSize, 50) because an old constant MaxPageSize=50 was never raised when the public docs moved to 100.
Likely a mismatch between the OpenAPI maximum and the hard-coded clamp in listSubscriptions. Cursor generation still works, so clients must issue extra round-trips without knowing why.
Large workspaces with many subscriptions take twice the calls to list them all.
comments: Docs say max 100; code says 50. Aligning code to 100 and adding a test that pageSize=100 returns 100 when enough rows exist.

issues.summary: Rate limiting counts OPTIONS preflight requests against the client quota
description: CORS preflight OPTIONS requests count against the same rate-limit quota as the real API calls. Browser apps that preflight frequently burn through the client's budget before the meaningful methods run.

Expected: OPTIONS for CORS is exempt from application quota (or billed to a separate generous bucket). Actual: each preflight decrements the same redis counter keyed by API token, so a chatty SPA can 429 on GET after a burst of OPTIONS alone.

Hypothesis: the rate-limit middleware runs before the CORS short-circuit, so OPTIONS never hits the bypass branch that skips quota for health checks. Method allowlisting for quota exemption omits OPTIONS.
Browser integrations look flaky under load tests even when server-side call volume is modest.
comments: Middleware order dump confirms rate limit wraps CORS. OPTIONS is counted.
Adding OPTIONS to the quota exempt method set and a metric for exempted preflights.
Staging SPA load test no longer 429s on preflight-heavy bursts. Waiting on one more review before prod.

issues.summary: SDK createIssue drops custom field values when the field is multi-select
description: SDK createIssue drops values for multi-select custom fields. The field is present in the request object, but the serialized payload either omits it or sends an empty array, so the issue is created without those selections.

Expected: multi-select custom fields accept an array of option ids and persist them on create. Actual: the v2 serializer treats multi-select like single-select and takes only a string path; arrays fail the type guard and the field is stripped before the HTTP send.

Hypothesis: CustomFieldValue union in the SDK still models multi-select as string rather than string[], a leftover from when the API only allowed single values. Server API has accepted arrays since 2.2.
Migration scripts and intake forms that set multi-select metadata create incomplete issues and require manual edits.
comments: Initial fix in 2.5.2 widened the type; unit tests passed with array values.
Released 2.5.2 and confirmed createIssue in staging kept multi-select options on the created issue.

Regression: partner reports that option ids passed as numbers still get dropped after coercion — array of numbers fails the string[] guard. Reopening until we coerce numeric ids or document string-only.

issues.summary: Worker dead-letter requeue loses the original attempt count metadata
description: When a job exhausts its delivery budget and lands in the dead-letter queue, the requeue path rebuilds the envelope from the DLQ record alone. Operators who then push the job back onto the live queue see attempt_count reset to 0 even though the DLQ row still holds attempt_count=7 and first_failed_at from the original run.

Expected requeue to copy attempt_count, max_attempts, and first_failed_at into the new queue message so downstream dashboards and circuit-breaker logic keep continuity. Actual behavior only restores job_id, payload, and topic; the attempt fields are re-initialized by the publisher defaults.

Suspected cause: dlq_requeue() serializes a fresh JobHeader via DefaultHeader() instead of unmarshaling the stored header blob, so the attempt metadata never leaves cold storage. Impact is skewed retry metrics and premature permanent-failure classification on the second cycle after requeue.
comments: Confirmed on the export-pdf topic: after requeue, attempt_count was 0 while the DLQ archive row still showed 7.
Root cause matched the DefaultHeader guess — requeue now deep-copies header_json from the DLQ row before republish.
Verified with a forced 5-fail job: requeued message kept attempt_count=5 and first_failed_at within 2s of the original stamp.

issues.summary: REST API CORS allowlist rejects legitimate subdomains of example.com
description: Clients calling https://api.tenant.example.com from https://app.tenant.example.com receive a CORS rejection even though *.example.com was added to the allowlist in the admin console. Preflight OPTIONS succeeds for the apex host but fails for any multi-label subdomain under the same registered domain.

The matcher splits the Origin host on dots and only compares the final two labels against each allowlist entry. That treats app.tenant.example.com as unrelated to an entry of example.com or *.example.com when the rule was stored without an explicit leading wildcard token.

Expectation is that an allowlist entry of example.com (or *.example.com) covers every subdomain depth under that registrable domain. Actual responses include Access-Control-Allow-Origin missing and a console error on the SPA bootstrap call to GET /v2/me.
Likely bug is in cors.MatchOrigin: it uses strings.HasSuffix against a single-dot suffix instead of publicsuffix-aware suffix matching, so three-or-more label hosts never pass.
comments: Reproduced with Origin https://preview.staging.example.com against allowlist entry example.com — browser blocked the response.
Switched matcher to publicsuffix.EffectiveTLDPlusOne plus an explicit *.<domain> branch; staging smoke passed for four subdomain depths.
Customer on NMS-4418 confirmed their app.tenant.example.com dashboard loads again after the 2.4.11 deploy.

issues.summary: Webhook test delivery endpoint always returns 200 even when the target is down
description: POST /v2/webhooks/{id}/test always responds with HTTP 200 and body {"delivered": true} regardless of whether the configured target URL is reachable. Pointing a subscription at https://hooks.example.com/unreachable still yields the success envelope within ~40ms.

Product expectation for the test endpoint is to perform a real signed POST, wait up to the 8s delivery timeout, and return the upstream status code plus our delivery_id. Operators currently cannot distinguish a healthy target from a dead one without tailing worker logs.

The handler appears to enqueue a fire-and-forget DeliveryJob and return before the worker reports outcome. Response mapping never inspects delivery_attempts.last_status, so the HTTP layer hard-codes 200.
Affects onboarding: new integrations mark the connection green even when the partner endpoint is misconfigured, delaying real incident discovery until the first production event fails.
comments: Tracing shows TestDeliveryHandler returns right after enqueue; no wait on the attempt result channel.
Adding a sync path with a 10s deadline and mapping upstream 5xx/timeouts to our 502/504. Draft PR open.
Still need to decide whether a refused TCP connection should surface as 502 or a structured 422 with reason=target_unreachable.

issues.summary: Pagination total count drifts when filters include labels with special characters
description: Listing issues with a label filter that contains plus, slash, or unicode punctuation returns a page of items whose length does not match the total field. Example: label=ci/cd+nightly yields 12 rows on page 1 but total=0, while the unfiltered count for the same project is 847.

The count query URL-decodes the label once before binding, but the data query goes through a second decode in the filter builder. Labels with reserved characters end up as different strings in the two SQL paths, so COUNT(*) and the LIMIT/OFFSET select disagree.
Clients that drive progress bars from total then show empty or complete states incorrectly. Workaround is to omit total and page until the last empty page, which is expensive for large projects.
comments: Not yet confirmed whether comma-separated multi-label filters hit the same double-decode path.

issues.summary: SDK retry middleware does not honor 503 Retry-After delay values
description: The official SDK retry middleware treats any 503 as a signal to apply the configured exponential backoff (base 250ms, cap 4s) and ignores the Retry-After header when the server sends a delta-seconds value. Under coordinated maintenance we emit Retry-After: 12, yet the client still hammers /v2/search every few hundred milliseconds.

Spec for the middleware says numeric Retry-After must set the next sleep to at least that many seconds before the usual jitter. Observed sleeps stay under 1s across five consecutive 503s in the integration harness.

Hypothesis: parseRetryAfter only handles HTTP-date form and returns zero for pure integers, after which the backoff branch never substitutes the server hint. Reopened after 1.9.2 claimed a fix — the unit test only covered the HTTP-date branch.
Customers with aggressive concurrency see amplified 503 storms and longer outages when we intentionally shed load.
comments: Integer parser was added in 1.9.2 but gated behind a case-sensitive map lookup after keys were lowercased, so Retry-After: 15 never reached the sleep path.
Regression suite now covers delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms; 1.9.3-rc.1 was cut with that suite green in CI.
Reproduced again on 1.9.3-rc.1 against staging: client waited 400ms instead of the 12s Retry-After we injected. Filing as reopened.

issues.summary: Worker concurrency semaphore leaks slots after a panicked handler
description: A handler that panics during Execute leaves the concurrency semaphore permanently acquired. After roughly 64 panics on a worker with max_inflight=64, the process stops accepting new jobs while CPU and memory look idle and the lease renewer is still healthy.

Expected path: recover in the outer run loop releases the slot via defer, then records the panic to the DLQ. Actual path acquires the weighted semaphore before installing the recover defer, so a panic between acquire and defer registration (or inside a non-deferred unlock helper) never returns the weight.

Root cause was acquireSlot() returning a release func that callers were expected to defer, but the panic wrapper called release only on the success and error returns — not on recover. Once max_inflight slots leaked, only a process restart restored throughput.
Hit overnight on the media-thumbnail pool after a nil-pointer regression in an image library upgrade.
comments: Metrics showed inflight_slots=64 and jobs_started flat for 40 minutes; no new leases taken.
Moved semaphore release into a defer immediately after acquire; panic path now always frees the weight.
Load test: 200 forced panics kept inflight_slots oscillating 0–8 instead of climbing to the cap.

issues.summary: REST field metadata endpoint caches deleted custom fields for the full TTL
description: GET /v2/field-metadata continues to list custom fields for up to the full 15-minute cache TTL after an admin deletes them. Clients that cache the response themselves then show pickers for fields that return 404 on write.

Delete handler removes the row from custom_fields but only busts the per-project key fieldmeta:{project_id}. Global and workspace-scoped entries fieldmeta:ws:{id} keep serving the pre-delete snapshot until natural expiry.

Reopened because the first fix busted project keys only; workspace-level metadata used by multi-project boards still served ghosts for the remaining TTL. Expectation is immediate consistency on delete for every cache key that included that field_id.
comments: Still seeing deleted field cf_custom_priority on a workspace board 12 minutes after delete — reopening.

issues.summary: Rate limiter redis key collision occurs across staging and production clusters
description: Staging and production API clusters share a Redis logical database for historical reasons and form rate-limit keys as rl:{api_key_hash}:{window}. A load test in staging that exhausts a key hash identical to a production token shape can throttle real traffic if the hash collides, and staging resets have cleared production counters overnight.
Keys must be cluster-scoped (e.g. rl:{env}:{api_key_hash}:{window}) or use separate Redis DBs. Today neither env var RATE_LIMIT_KEY_PREFIX nor the deployment name is folded into the key material.

During last Thursday's staging soak we observed production 429 rates jump ~3x for tokens whose SHA-256 prefix matched fixtures in the load script. No data corruption, but customer-facing throttling from a non-prod workload is unacceptable.
comments: Confirmed both clusters point at redis://shared-rl.example.com:6379/0 with the same key template.
Proposal: inject env into the key and migrate production to DB 2 this week — need a brief dual-write window.

issues.summary: Webhook payload omits the previous status when the transition skips intermediate states
description: When an issue jumps from To Do straight to Done via a workflow transition that skips In Progress, the issue.updated webhook body sets status to Done but leaves previous_status null (or omits the field). Consumers that drive automations on status deltas cannot tell what the prior state was.

Normal single-step transitions correctly populate previous_status from the transition's from_status_id. Multi-hop or admin "move to" paths load only the destination status into the event builder and never read issues.status before the update commit.

Hypothesis: StatusTransitionEvent is built after the UPDATE, and the skip path uses a bulk status writer that does not pass old_status into the outbox payload. Fix should snapshot status in the same transaction before write, regardless of intermediate skips.
Integrations that gate on leaving In Progress silently no-op for these jumps, which is how the report surfaced.
comments: Captured a raw payload where changelog showed To Do→Done but webhook previous_status was absent.
Looking at bulk_status_writer vs single transition path — only the latter attaches old_status to the outbox row.

issues.summary: SDK TypeScript types mark required create fields as optional after codegen
description: After running the OpenAPI codegen for SDK 2.1, TypeScript interfaces for create payloads mark project_key, summary, and issue_type as optional even though the API returns 400 without them. Call sites that relied on compile-time required checks now type-check with empty objects.

The generator maps all schema properties through a nullable-union helper that strips required[] when any property uses allOf wrappers. CreateIssueRequest is defined with allOf + required, and the helper drops the required list while merging.

Expectation: fields listed in the OpenAPI required array remain non-optional in the emitted .d.ts. Actual: every create body field is T | undefined, so strict clients ship incomplete requests that only fail at runtime.
comments: Diffed openapi.json: required is still present; the drop happens in our allOf flatten step.
Trying openapi-typescript 7.x merge strategy vs our fork — fork is the one clearing required.

issues.summary: Worker job IDs collide when two nodes boot within the same millisecond
description: Job IDs are composed as {node_id_hex}-{millis_since_epoch}-{counter}. When two worker nodes finish boot in the same millisecond and both start counters at 0, the first jobs they enqueue can share an identical job_id if node_id assignment also collides during a brief membership flap.

More commonly, node_id is derived from a truncated MAC hash that collides under certain cloud NIC renames, so the millisecond+counter pair alone is not unique. Duplicate primary keys on job_events then cause the second insert to fail and the job to be dropped after the publish ack.

A safer scheme would use a 128-bit random id or include a process start ulid segment that is unique per process lifetime. Current collision window is small but has produced at least three lost jobs in the last 30 days on the EU pool.

issues.summary: REST API accepts empty assignee_slot strings instead of returning 400
description: PUT /v2/issues/{id} accepts assignee_slot: "" and stores an empty string instead of rejecting the body. Downstream assignment UIs treat empty string as a distinct slot from null, showing a blank chip that cannot be cleared without a raw API call.

Validation already rejects whitespace-only display names and unknown slot tokens, but the empty string bypasses the enum check because the binder coerces "" to a present optional before the non-empty rule runs.
Expected: 400 with code field_invalid and message that assignee_slot must be a non-empty slot id or omitted/null to unassign. Actual: 200 with assignee_slot saved as "".
comments: Easy validation fix; want product to confirm null vs omit for unassign before we ship.

issues.summary: Webhook fan-out delivers events twice when the subscription uses two endpoints
description: A single webhook subscription configured with two endpoint URLs receives each event twice on both endpoints (four HTTP deliveries total) instead of once per endpoint. Fan-out should produce N deliveries for N endpoints, not N×N.

The dispatcher iterates endpoints and, for each, reloads the full endpoint list from the subscription snapshot before enqueue. Nested iteration multiplies the set: with 2 endpoints the inner loop runs twice per outer step.
Discovered via partner logs showing duplicate delivery_id pairs differing only by a trailing endpoint index that was applied twice. No data loss on our side, but partner automations double-executed.

issues.summary: Expose a public endpoint to list webhook delivery attempts for a subscription
description: Support and integrators currently need internal admin tools or log access to inspect whether a given webhook subscription delivered, retried, or exhausted a specific event. That slows incident response when a partner claims they never received issue.updated.

Expose GET /v2/webhooks/{subscription_id}/deliveries with filters for event_type, status (success|failed|pending), and created_after. Each item should include attempt_number, http_status, latency_ms, response_snippet (truncated), and next_retry_at.

Acceptance: a project admin token can list the last 7 days of attempts for subscriptions they own; responses are paginated with cursor; secrets and full response bodies are never returned; rate limited to 30 req/min per token.
comments: Draft OpenAPI fragment up; debating whether response_snippet is 256 or 512 bytes.
Authz check will reuse subscription ownership from the existing GET subscription route.

issues.summary: Allow SDK consumers to stream search results via async iterators
description: Large search result sets force SDK users to hand-roll offset or cursor loops, which is error-prone around rate limits and cancellation. Native async iteration would match how many runtimes already consume streams.
Add client.issues.searchStream(query) that yields Issue objects via AsyncIterable, internally advancing the cursor from each page's next_cursor until exhausted or the abort signal fires.

Acceptance: works in Node 18+ and modern browsers; respects the client's retry middleware; documents backpressure as best-effort (pull-based); unit tests cover empty pages, single page, and mid-stream 429 recovery.

issues.summary: Support soft rate-limit warnings at 80 percent of the hourly quota
description: Hard 429s at 100% of the hourly quota surprise clients that could have shed load earlier. Several partners asked for a predictive signal before the hard ceiling.
When usage crosses 80% of the hourly budget, include RateLimit-Warning: 80-percent with remaining and reset timestamps on otherwise successful responses. Do not change status codes or body shapes.

Acceptance: warning appears only on authenticated routes that already emit RateLimit-Remaining; warning clears after the window rolls; documented in the public rate-limit guide; feature-flagged for a one-week canary.
comments: Product signed off on 80% as the sole threshold for v1 — no multi-tier warnings yet.

issues.summary: Let workers publish progress checkpoints for multi-minute export jobs
description: Multi-minute CSV/JSON exports leave the UI with a spinner and no intermediate feedback. Support tickets spike when users refresh and start a second export.

Workers writing export jobs may POST progress checkpoints {percent, rows_done, rows_estimated, updated_at} to an internal progress channel every ~5 seconds or every 2k rows, whichever comes first. The jobs API surfaces the latest checkpoint on GET /v2/jobs/{id}.
Acceptance: a 500k-row export updates percent at least 10 times before completion; failed jobs retain the last checkpoint; checkpoints older than 24h are pruned with the job row.
comments: Implemented checkpoint writer with min interval 4s to avoid Redis chatter.
UI team wired a progress bar against GET job; looks good on staging exports of 120k rows.
Shipped in workers 3.12; closing after 48h of stable production metrics.

issues.summary: Add a REST filter for issues updated since a specific cursor token
description: Sync agents that poll for recently changed issues currently approximate "since" with updated_at timestamps, which misses clock skew and double-delivers rows updated in the same second.

Add query parameter updated_since_cursor on GET /v2/issues that accepts an opaque token returned from a previous page or from X-Issues-Cursor on list responses. Server decodes to a (updated_at, issue_id) pair for stable keyset pagination.
Acceptance: cursor is monotonic across concurrent updates; invalid tokens return 400; documentation includes a sample poll loop; works with existing project and label filters.

issues.summary: Provide signed temporary URLs for large attachment downloads in the SDK
description: Attachment download currently streams through the API gateway, which caps throughput and holds worker connections for multi-hundred-MB files. Edge and mobile clients need a short-lived direct URL.
SDK method attachments.getDownloadUrl(id, {ttlSeconds}) should call a new REST route that returns a signed HTTPS URL valid between 60 and 900 seconds, plus content_type and byte_size.

Acceptance: URL requires no API key at the storage edge; revoked attachments fail with 404 on sign; SDK throws on ttl outside range; documented threat model notes that anyone with the URL can download until expiry.

issues.summary: Allow webhook filters by project key and issue type without a separate subscription
description: Teams that only care about bugs in project ALPHA currently create separate subscriptions or filter in their own service. That multiplies secrets and delivery noise for high-volume workspaces.
Allow a single subscription to declare include_project_keys and include_issue_types arrays. Events that fail the filter are dropped before fan-out and do not count against delivery quota.
Acceptance: empty arrays mean no restriction; unknown project keys rejected at write time; changing filters does not drop in-flight deliveries; OpenAPI and webhook console UI updated together.
comments: Backlog candidate for next webhook epic; no commitment this quarter yet.

issues.summary: Surface remaining rate-limit budget on every successful authenticated response
description: Clients today only learn remaining budget when they finally hit 429 or when they call a separate quota endpoint. Embedding budget on success responses lets them pace batches without extra round-trips.
On every successful authenticated response, emit RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset (unix seconds) consistent with the hourly window that applied to that route class.
Acceptance: header values match the Redis counter within one request of race; unauthenticated public GETs omit the headers; changelog entry and SDK response wrapper expose remaining as a number.
comments: Middleware draft attaches headers post-handler so 4xx validation errors still include remaining when auth succeeded.
Need to confirm whether search's heavier cost multiplier should show effective remaining or raw counter units.

issues.summary: Add a dry-run mode for bulk mutation endpoints that returns a change plan
description: Bulk edit and bulk transition endpoints are hard to validate safely against production-shaped data. Partners want a preview of what would change without committing writes.

Support dry_run=true on POST /v2/issues/bulk-update and /v2/issues/bulk-transition. Response returns a change plan: matched_count, would_update_count, sample of up to 20 issue ids with before/after field snapshots, and validation errors per id — no row mutations, no webhooks.
Acceptance: dry_run requests do not increment write audit logs as mutations; authorization is identical to the real path; plan generation finishes within 5s for up to 500 matched issues.

issues.summary: Let SDK clients configure a custom fetch implementation for edge runtimes
description: Edge runtimes (Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy) cannot use the default global fetch binding the SDK closes over at module init, or they need undici-compatible stubs with custom cert handling.
Allow NimbusClient options.fetch to supply any fetch-compatible function; all HTTP calls in the SDK must go through that hook, including retries and streaming helpers.
Acceptance: documented example for a custom fetch; default remains globalThis.fetch; type definitions accept typeof fetch; integration test injects a mock that records URLs.

issues.summary: Support idempotency keys on create endpoints for at-most-once client retries
description: Mobile and flaky networks often retry POST /v2/issues and create duplicates when the first request succeeded but the response was lost. Clients need at-most-once semantics without building their own dedupe store.

Accept header Idempotency-Key (UUIDv4 recommended) on create endpoints. First request stores the response body and status for 24h keyed by (api_key_id, idempotency_key); replays return the stored response without re-executing side effects.
Acceptance: conflicting body hash for the same key returns 409; keys expire after 24h; documented for issues, comments, and webhook subscriptions create routes.
comments: Storage backed by Redis with payload in object store for bodies > 8KB.
Conflict path verified: same key, different summary → 409 idempotency_key_reuse.
Docs live; marking done after two partner SDKs adopted the header.

issues.summary: Expose worker queue depth metrics via a read-only ops endpoint
description: On-call currently scrapes worker logs or Redis CLI to judge backlog severity. A stable ops signal is needed for dashboards and autoscaling.
Add GET /v2/ops/worker-queues (ops-scoped token only) returning per-queue depth, oldest_job_age_seconds, and inflight for each named topic. Read-only, no job payloads.
Acceptance: authorized ops tokens only (403 otherwise); p99 latency under 100ms; metrics match Redis LLEN within a 2s skew; runbook updated.
comments: Endpoint shipped behind OPS_READ scope.
Grafana board points at it; closed after a week of matching hand-checked depths.

issues.summary: Allow partial field updates on issues without replacing the full body
description: PATCH was missing for issues, so clients had to PUT the full resource and risked clobbering concurrent edits to unrelated fields.

Support PATCH /v2/issues/{id} with a partial JSON object; only provided fields are validated and written. Unset fields remain unchanged. Use merge semantics for maps like custom_fields (shallow merge by key).
Acceptance: patching summary alone does not clear description; unknown fields 400; ETag / If-Match still enforced; OpenAPI and SDK updated.
comments: Implementation reuses the field-level validators from PUT.
Concurrency test with two PATCHers on different fields both succeed with sequential versions.
Released in API 2.5.0.

issues.summary: Add SDK helpers for building JQL-like filters with typed field names
description: Hand-built JQL-like filter strings in application code are a common source of escaping bugs and typos on field names.

Ship SDK helpers such as filters.and(filters.eq('status', 'Done'), filters.contains('labels', 'backend')) that produce the wire filter AST the search API already accepts, with TypeScript/Python typed field name unions generated from field metadata.
Acceptance: helpers cover eq, neq, in, contains, gt/lt on dates; output matches hand-written filters in golden tests; no runtime dependency on a full JQL parser.

issues.summary: Support rotating webhook secrets with a dual-validation grace period
description: Rotating a webhook secret today is a hard cutover: partners must update verifiers at the same instant we switch signing keys, which causes signature failures during deploys.

Support setting a next_secret while current_secret remains valid. For a configurable grace period (default 48h), deliveries are signed with next_secret and verification on our test endpoint accepts either secret. After grace, current is replaced and next cleared.
Acceptance: admin API to begin/commit/cancel rotation; delivery headers include X-Nimbus-Signature-Version so consumers know which key was used; audit log entries for each rotation step.
comments: Working through dual-sign vs sign-with-next-only — leaning sign-with-next, verify-both for partner simplicity.
Grace default 48h approved by security review draft.

issues.summary: Let API keys be scoped to a subset of projects and HTTP methods
description: Workspace-wide API keys are too broad for contractors and CI jobs that should only touch a few projects or only read.
Allow API keys to declare project_ids allowlist and allowed_methods (subset of GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE). Requests outside the scope return 403 with code key_scope_violation.
Acceptance: empty project list means all projects (backward compatible); method list required at create; existing keys migrate as unrestricted; admin UI can edit scope without rotating the secret.
comments: Enforcement sits in the auth middleware after key lookup.
Migration backfill marked unrestricted; docs published.
Closing — two enterprise tenants already scoped their CI keys to single projects.

issues.summary: Provide a bulk reindex endpoint that reports per-project completion status
description: Search index rebuilds after schema changes are triggered per project via support tools. Customers with many projects need a self-serve bulk kickoff and visibility into which projects finished.

POST /v2/admin/reindex with project_keys[] (or all=true for workspace admins) enqueues reindex jobs and returns a run_id. GET /v2/admin/reindex/{run_id} lists per-project status: queued, running, done, failed, with counts and error summaries.
Acceptance: cannot start a second overlapping all=true run; failed projects are retryable via POST .../retry; progress visible within 10s of worker updates.

issues.summary: Allow workers to pause and resume long-running jobs without losing lease state
description: Long export and reindex jobs are sometimes intentionally paused for maintenance windows, but today pause cancels the lease and the job restarts from scratch or is marked failed.

Workers should support pause and resume control messages that freeze progress, renew a paused lease with a longer TTL, and on resume continue from the last checkpoint without reprocessing completed partitions.
Acceptance: pause is idempotent; resume fails clearly if the checkpoint is missing; paused jobs do not count toward concurrency slots; ops endpoint shows paused state and lease expiry.
comments: Lease schema draft adds state=paused and pause_reason.
Spike on export worker looks feasible because checkpoints already exist from NMA-121 work.

issues.summary: Add integration tests for the bulk import worker pagination edge cases
description: Bulk import worker pagination has had three production incidents around empty final pages, page sizes larger than remaining rows, and source cursors that rewind after a 503. Coverage today is mostly unit tests on pure helpers.

Done when an integration suite spins a fake source API and asserts: empty last page completes the job; mid-stream 503 retries without duplicating imported issue keys; page_size=1 and page_size=500 both reach terminal success; metrics counters for pages_fetched match expectations.
comments: Scaffolding testcontainers + wiremock for the source side.
Empty last page case already red — matches the last incident.

issues.summary: Document rate limit tiers and header semantics for public API consumers
description: Public docs mention rate limits only in passing and omit header names, window length, and per-route cost multipliers. Partners reverse-engineer behavior from 429 bodies.

Complete when the developer portal has a dedicated page covering free/pro/enterprise hourly tiers, RateLimit-* headers, 429 JSON shape, Retry-After behavior, and cost weights for search vs write routes, reviewed by DX and linked from the API reference.
comments: First draft in the docs repo; engineering reviewed header table.
Published under /docs/rate-limits; redirect from the old FAQ blurb is live.

issues.summary: Migrate webhook delivery logs to a partitioned cold-storage table
description: webhook_delivery_logs is a single hot table past 400M rows; vacuum and index maintenance stall writers during peak. Query patterns are almost always time-bounded by created_at.

Migrate to monthly range partitions on created_at, detach partitions older than 90 days to cold storage object dumps, and keep a thin hot parent for the recent window. Completion means dual-write validation for one week, cutover runbook executed in staging then production, and app queries unchanged via the parent table name.
comments: Partition DDL ready; backfill of the last 3 months into partitions running on a replica first.
App still points at the monolithic table — cutover PR waits on backfill checksum.

issues.summary: Generate SDK release notes from the OpenAPI diff for each minor version
description: SDK changelogs were hand-written and often missed OpenAPI-only additions. Consumers need accurate minor-version notes without relying on tribal knowledge.

Done when CI on the SDK repo runs an OpenAPI diff against the previous minor tag and generates a markdown release-notes fragment (added/removed/changed operations and schemas) attached to the GitHub release and npm package README section.
comments: Script lives in tools/openapi-changelog; wired into the release workflow.
Validated on the 2.0→2.1 cut — notes matched the manual list plus two forgotten schema enum values.

issues.summary: Instrument REST 4xx/5xx ratios with project-key dimensions
description: REST error traffic is only visible as global counts today, which hides which project keys drive most 4xx and 5xx responses during incidents.
Add instrumentation that records 4xx and 5xx ratios with a project-key dimension so on-call can slice dashboards by tenant without replaying logs.
Keep cardinality bounded by hashing unknown keys into an other bucket and document the metric names for the platform observability wiki.

issues.summary: Replace ad-hoc sleep retries with the shared exponential backoff package
description: Several SDK modules still retry network failures with fixed Thread.sleep loops that ignore jitter and total deadline budgets.
Replace those ad-hoc sleeps with the shared exponential backoff package already used by the CLI so retry policy stays consistent across languages.
Preserve existing public retry hook callbacks and add a unit test that proves backoff doubles up to the configured ceiling.
comments: Inventory of call sites is ready in the SDK retry audit spreadsheet; three modules still need migration.

issues.summary: Add contract tests for webhook signature verification across secret rotations
description: Webhook signature verification is covered by happy-path unit tests only, so secret rotation windows are untested.
Add contract tests that rotate signing secrets mid-suite, accept requests signed with the previous secret within the grace period, and reject them after expiry.
Cover both HMAC header styles we document for external partners on example.com callback endpoints.

issues.summary: Backfill missing created_at indexes on the worker job history table
description: The worker job history table lacks created_at indexes on several shards, so retention cleanup scans full partitions during peak hours.
Backfill the missing indexes online with a throttled migration that pauses when replica lag exceeds the agreed threshold.
Validate query plans for the cleanup job and the history browser after each shard completes.
comments: Migration script drafted against staging; running explain analyze on the first two shards tonight.
Replica lag stay under 2s with batch size 5k so far; continuing on the remaining regions.

issues.summary: Remove deprecated v1 list endpoints still referenced in internal docs
description: Deprecated v1 list endpoints remain registered for compatibility even though public clients moved to v2 months ago.
Remove the handlers, update internal docs that still deep-link to the old paths, and return a clear gone response only if any residual traffic appears.
Confirm gateway access logs show zero production hits for a full week before the final delete ships.
comments: Docs PR merged; only the engineering handbook still mentioned v1 list routes.
One week of zero hits confirmed in access metrics; endpoints removed in release 3.14.

issues.summary: Add chaos tests for rate limiter redis failover behavior
description: Rate limiter behavior during Redis failover is only verified manually after incidents.
Add chaos tests that kill the primary Redis node mid-burst and assert fail-open versus fail-closed modes match configuration for each limiter class.
Record recovery time and duplicate allow decisions so we can set SLOs for the rate limiting control plane.

issues.summary: Extract common cursor encoding helpers shared by list and search routes
description: List and search routes each implement their own cursor encoding, which has drifted on null handling and sort-key escaping.
Extract shared helpers for encoding and decoding opaque cursors and route both families through them.
Add golden fixtures for multi-field sort keys so pagination stays stable across releases.
comments: Proposed package path under rest/pagination; waiting on review of the null sentinel choice.

issues.summary: Upgrade the SDK HTTP client to enforce TLS 1.2 minimum
description: The SDK HTTP client still allows TLS 1.0 and 1.1 on older language runtimes, which fails enterprise security scans.
Upgrade the client defaults to require TLS 1.2 minimum and surface a clear error when the runtime cannot negotiate it.
Document the change in the SDK migration notes for customers pinning ancient OpenSSL builds.

issues.summary: Write a runbook for replaying failed webhook deliveries from the DLQ
description: Operators currently re-drive failed webhook deliveries by querying the dead-letter queue with ad-hoc scripts.
Write a runbook that covers locating failed deliveries, replaying by delivery id or time window, and verifying partner receipt on example.com sandbox endpoints.
Include rollback steps when a replay storm would exceed partner rate limits.
comments: First draft reviewed by on-call; added screenshots of the DLQ console filters.
Published under ops/webhooks/replay-dlq and linked from the incident playbook index.

issues.summary: Add benchmark fixtures for the search index rebuild worker
description: Search index rebuild performance is hard to compare across changes because fixtures are hand-built and tiny.
Add benchmark fixtures that mirror production document shape distributions for the rebuild worker, including nested custom fields and large comment threads.
Wire the fixtures into a nightly job that reports wall time and peak memory so regressions are visible before release.

issues.summary: Normalize error response envelopes across REST and webhook test endpoints
description: REST error bodies and webhook test endpoint errors use different envelope shapes, which confuses shared client generators.
Normalize error response envelopes so both surfaces expose code, message, details, and request id in the same structure.
Update contract tests and the public error catalog page once the shape is frozen.
comments: Agreed schema in the API working group notes; implementation landed behind a compatibility flag first.
Flag defaulted on after two weeks with no partner breakage reports.

issues.summary: Delete unused protobuf stubs from the pre-v2 worker protocol
description: Pre-v2 worker protocol protobuf stubs remain in the monorepo even though no service loads them at runtime.
Delete the unused stubs, regenerate any residual imports, and shrink the worker image layer that still packaged the old descriptors.
Confirm CI no longer runs protoc targets for the retired package.
comments: Stub package removed; one stray import in a test helper fixed in the same change.
Image size dropped about 4MB; CI target list cleaned up.

issues.summary: Add feature flags for the soft rate-limit warning headers experiment
description: The soft rate-limit warning headers experiment needs controlled rollout rather than a global config flip.
Add feature flags that enable warning headers per project or plan tier and emit whether the header was sent for analysis.
Default the experiment off in production until the analytics dashboard is wired.
comments: Flag keys proposed as rate_limit.soft_warn_headers with project override support.

issues.summary: Document SDK authentication flows for OAuth and API key side by side
description: SDK authentication docs describe OAuth and API keys in separate pages that contradict each other on token refresh behavior.
Document both flows side by side with a comparison table, shared troubleshooting section, and example.com callback samples for OAuth redirects.
Call out which environments allow API keys versus interactive OAuth only.

issues.summary: Create load-test scenarios for concurrent bulk updates of 10k issues
description: Bulk update paths have not been load-tested at the 10k concurrent issue scale customers request for migrations.
Create load-test scenarios that issue concurrent bulk updates of 10k issues, measure p95 latency and conflict rates, and assert no silent partial commits.
Store scenario definitions next to the existing REST load suite so release candidates can re-run them.
comments: k6 scripts committed; staging run hit target concurrency without 5xx spikes.
Documented baseline numbers in the capacity planning folder for the next scale review.

issues.summary: Refactor worker lease renewal into a shared library used by all job types
description: Each job type reimplements worker lease renewal with slightly different timeout math and heartbeats.
Refactor lease renewal into a shared library used by all job types, with one configuration surface for interval, jitter, and max extension.
Migrate job packages one at a time behind a feature gate until every type uses the shared path.
comments: Shared library extracted; export and search jobs migrated first.
Remaining job types completed this sprint; old local renewal helpers deleted.
On-call confirmed lease expiry alerts stayed quiet during the cutover window.

issues.summary: Add OpenTelemetry traces around webhook fan-out fan-in paths
description: Webhook fan-out and fan-in paths lack distributed traces, so multi-hop delivery delays are hard to attribute.
Add OpenTelemetry traces around fan-out dispatch and fan-in aggregation, including delivery id and destination host attributes.
Sample aggressively in staging and at the standard production rate so dashboards remain affordable.
comments: Spans wired through the dispatcher and aggregator; verified parent links in the staging collector.
Production rollout complete; runbook updated with example trace queries.

issues.summary: Migrate internal service tokens off static secrets to short-lived JWTs
description: Internal service tokens for workers still rely on long-lived static secrets stored in the secret manager.
Migrate workers to short-lived JWTs issued by the internal identity service, with automatic refresh before expiry.
Rotate out static secrets after all worker fleets present JWTs and revoke the old credentials.
comments: JWT client library integrated in the worker bootstrap path.
Staging fleet fully on JWTs; production canary at 20% with no auth failures.
Next step is region-by-region production cutover starting with us-west.

issues.summary: Ship a redaction policy for PII fields in worker debug logs
description: Worker debug logs occasionally include raw email addresses and phone numbers when jobs dump payloads on failure.
Ship a redaction policy that masks known PII field paths before debug logging and fails closed if a new field is marked sensitive without a rule.
Audit a week of sampled logs after rollout to confirm no unredacted matches remain.
comments: Policy table and default maskers merged; debug flag now routes through the redactor.
Post-rollout sample found zero unmasked emails in the checked windows.

issues.summary: Add schema validation for incoming webhook filter expressions
description: Incoming webhook filter expressions are stored as opaque strings and only fail when delivery runs.
Add schema validation at registration time so invalid operators and unknown fields are rejected with field-level errors.
Preserve existing valid filters via a one-time validation pass before enforcing on write.
comments: JSON schema drafted against the filter grammar doc.
Enforcement enabled after the backfill reported zero invalid existing filters.

issues.summary: Customer cannot download invoice after plan change mid-cycle
description: After a mid-cycle plan change, some customers cannot download the current invoice from the Billing Questions portal action.
The download button returns a generic failure and the browser network tab shows a 404 for the invoice PDF resource id generated at plan change time.
Reproduce with a sandbox account that upgrades mid-cycle, capture the resource id mapping, and fix generation so post-change invoices remain downloadable.
issues.environment: Billing portal production, Chrome 128 on macOS, plan change from Standard to Plus mid-cycle
comments: Support confirmed three example.com tenants hit this in the last billing cycle.

issues.summary: Support portal ticket status stuck on Waiting despite agent reply
description: Tickets in the support portal remain stuck on Waiting even after an agent posts a public reply that should move them to Pending customer or Open.
Status transition logs show the reply event without a matching status update when the ticket was previously Waiting on customer.
Identify the race between the reply writer and the status machine and ensure agent replies always advance status for portal-visible tickets.
issues.environment: Support portal production and staging, agent workspace desktop web
comments: Reproduced on staging with a Waiting ticket and a single public agent comment.
Likely related to the status cache introduced last sprint; checking cache invalidation order.

issues.summary: Escalation auto-assign skips the on-call rotation for EU overnight hours
description: Escalation auto-assign skipped the EU overnight on-call rotation and assigned tickets to the previous daytime owner.
Rotation schedule entries for EU overnight were present but the assigner used UTC day boundaries incorrectly when selecting the active shift.
Correct the timezone handling, add fixture coverage for overnight EU windows, and reassign any tickets misrouted during the affected nights.
issues.environment: Escalation service production, EU region schedules, overnight 22:00-06:00 Europe/Berlin
comments: Root cause confirmed as day-boundary math in the rotation picker.
Fix shipped; overnight EU escalations for the past week were reviewed and reassigned where needed.
Monitoring shows correct owners for the last three EU overnight windows.

issues.summary: Billing question form drops the attached screenshot on mobile Safari
description: On mobile Safari the Billing Questions form accepts a screenshot attachment in the UI but submits the ticket without the file.
Desktop browsers upload the same image successfully, pointing to a multipart boundary or file input reset issue on iOS Safari.
Fix the client upload path for mobile Safari and add a device-level check that blocks submit when the attachment preview is present but the file blob is missing.
issues.environment: iOS 17 Safari, Billing Questions form on support.example.com

issues.summary: Customer reports missing issues after workspace merge completed green
description: A customer reports issues missing from the target workspace after a workspace merge that completed with a green status.
Merge job logs show success counts that do not match the source issue inventory, suggesting skipped projects or a partial project remapping.
Audit the merge job for silent skip paths, restore missing issues from backups if needed, and fail the merge job when inventory checks do not reconcile.
comments: Customer workspace pair details collected; waiting on merge job id from the success email.

issues.summary: Triage queue sorts by last updated instead of first response SLA
description: The triage queue UI sorts tickets by last updated time instead of first response SLA remaining, so newest activity floats above breaches.
Agents miss SLA risk tickets that have not been touched recently because the default sort no longer matches the SLA board contract.
Restore first response SLA as the default sort, keep last updated as an optional column sort, and add a regression test for the default ordering.
issues.environment: Agent triage queue web app, production

issues.summary: Escalation email goes to the previous owner after a handoff
description: After an escalation handoff, notification email still goes to the previous owner instead of the new assignee.
The handoff updates the ticket owner field but the escalation mailer reads a cached owner snapshot from the escalation record.
Refresh the owner snapshot on handoff and resend any misdirected notifications identified in the audit window.
issues.environment: Escalation notifications production, SMTP path to agent mailboxes
comments: Bug confirmed with a scripted handoff in staging.
Fix deployed; mailer now joins live owner at send time.
Affected customers from the last two weeks notified via support.

issues.summary: Support macros insert outdated refund policy text from 2025
description: Support macros still insert refund policy text dated 2025 that legal retired after the policy refresh.
Agents using the macros send outdated refund windows and eligibility language to customers on the portal.
Update macro content to the current policy, add a review date field so stale macros surface in admin, and notify teams that reused the old text.
issues.environment: Support agent desktop, macro picker in ticket reply composer
comments: Content owners supplied the replacement policy paragraphs.
Macro catalog update in progress for Billing and General categories.

Recurrence: after the initial content fix, two macros in the EU language pack still expanded the 2025 refund clause when agents selected the localized refund template; purged the stale translations and added a CI check that fails if policy macros reference the retired year.

issues.summary: Customer SSO login fails only on the support portal subdomain
description: Customer SSO login succeeds on the main app domain but fails only on the support portal subdomain with a generic authentication error.
ACS URL configuration for the portal subdomain appears out of sync with the identity provider metadata customers download from example.com docs.
Align portal SAML endpoints with the documented ACS URLs, improve error messages for ACS mismatch, and provide a self-serve metadata check.
comments: Two enterprise tenants confirmed failure limited to support.example.com while app.example.com SSO works.

issues.summary: Billing proration explanation in the portal mismatches the invoice line items
description: The portal Billing Questions page explains proration with amounts that do not match the invoice line items for the same period.
Customers open tickets citing the mismatch even when the invoice itself is correct, driving avoidable support volume.
Recalculate the explanation widget from the same proration service used for invoice generation and add a snapshot test for mid-cycle upgrades.
comments: Widget used a simplified day-count formula while invoices use the billing engine rules.
Aligned the widget to the billing engine; verified against three historical invoices.
Closed after portal copy and numbers matched line items in production checks.

issues.summary: Triage labels applied via bulk action do not persist after refresh
description: Triage labels applied through bulk action appear immediately but disappear after a page refresh.
Single-ticket label edits persist correctly, isolating the issue to the bulk write path or its response handling.
Ensure bulk label mutations commit and invalidate list caches so refresh shows the same labels agents just applied.
issues.environment: Agent triage bulk actions, production web
comments: Bulk API returned 200 while the join table write was rolled back on partial project permission failures.
Fixed transactional boundaries and surface partial failures to the bulk UI.
Verified labels persist after refresh in production verification.

issues.summary: Escalation timer resets when a public comment is added by the customer
description: When a customer adds a public comment on an escalated ticket, the escalation timer resets to the full SLA window.
Timer reset should apply only to agent-owned clocks, not customer comments that should leave the escalation deadline unchanged.
Adjust timer rules, backfill incorrectly extended escalations still open, and cover the case in SLA unit tests.

issues.summary: Customer cannot reopen a closed ticket from the portal within 24 hours
description: Customers cannot reopen a closed ticket from the portal within the advertised 24-hour window; the reopen control is disabled or returns an error.
Server policy allows reopen for 24 hours but the portal client uses a stricter closed-at check based on local time without timezone normalization.
Fix the client window calculation, match server policy, and show remaining reopen time clearly on the closed ticket view.
comments: Support has workarounds by reopening from the agent side; portal path still broken for self-serve.

issues.summary: Billing questions route to Triage instead of Billing Questions queue
description: Tickets submitted through the Billing Questions form are routed into the general Triage queue instead of the Billing Questions queue.
Routing rules still key off an old form id after the form rebuild, so billing work waits behind unrelated triage volume.
Update the router mapping for the current form id, move misrouted open tickets, and add a canary assertion on form-to-queue binding.
issues.environment: Portal form routing production, Billing Questions intake

issues.summary: Support search returns tickets from other workspaces for shared domains
description: Support search returns tickets belonging to other workspaces when those workspaces share an email domain with the searching agent tenant.
Workspace isolation should scope search hits by workspace id regardless of shared domains on example.com customer contacts.
Tighten the search filter, add multi-workspace isolation tests, and audit recent cross-workspace search access logs.
issues.environment: Support search production, multi-workspace tenants sharing contact domains
comments: Security reviewed as confidentiality risk; prioritize before the next enterprise review.

issues.summary: Escalation severity dropdown loses the selected value on mobile web
description: On a phone-sized viewport the Escalation severity <select> accepts a tap, briefly shows the chosen rank (e.g. Sev-2), then snaps back to the empty placeholder the moment the picker closes. Reproduced on Chrome 141 for Android and Safari 18 on iOS; desktop widths never misbehave.

Agents expect the committed option to stay bound to the form field until they submit or change it again. Instead severity_id is cleared client-side, so the POST body ships null and the API falls back to the workspace default.

Hypothesis: the mobile sheet fires a synthetic blur before the change event, and our controlled-component handler reads the still-stale React state when rebuilding options from /escalations/severities. Because the option list is remounted on every blur, the previously selected key is dropped.
Impact is confined to mobile web agents creating or editing escalations; roughly two dozen NMS tickets this sprint arrived with the wrong severity and had to be corrected by a lead.
comments: Confirmed the blur-before-change ordering only on viewports under 768px; desktop mouse selection is fine.
Root cause was remounting the severity options array on blur. Pinned selection with a local severityDraft ref that only commits on explicit change.
Verified on a Pixel 8 (Chrome 141) and iPhone 15 (Safari 18): Sev-1 through Sev-4 stick after picker dismiss. Shipped in 2.18.4.

issues.summary: Customer attachment virus scan never completes for files over 8 MB
description: Attachments larger than 8 MB that land on a customer ticket never leave the virus_scan_pending state. Smaller files (we tested 3.2 MB and 7.9 MB PDFs) finish scanning in under 40 seconds and become downloadable; a 8.1 MB zip stays pending indefinitely.

Expected: the scan worker marks the object clean or quarantined and flips attachment.scan_status within a few minutes. Actual: the row stays pending, the agent UI shows a spinner forever, and the customer sees "scan in progress" with no retry path.

Likely cause is the scan client reusing a single signed GET URL whose expiry is hardcoded to 60 seconds while the AV worker streams the full object through ClamAV. For files past ~8 MB the download exceeds that window, the stream aborts mid-read, and the worker retries with the same expired cursor instead of minting a fresh URL.
NMS-facing: three enterprise accounts filed this in the last fortnight. Agents cannot share large diagnostic dumps until scan completes, so escalations stall.
comments: Traced worker logs for attachment_id att_9f2c: signed URL expired at T+60s while ClamAV was still at 61% of an 11 MB archive.
Trying a refactor that re-signs the object URL on each retry and raises the soft size ceiling used by the pending-timeout watchdog.
Customer on tenant nimbus-demo-west re-uploaded a 12 MB HAR this morning — still stuck pending after 90 minutes. Reopening because the partial fix never rolled to production EU.

issues.summary: Triage SLA breach banner shows for tickets already first-responded
description: The red "SLA breached — first response overdue" banner still appears on triage tickets whose first_response_at is already populated. Spotted on tickets that were answered via the mobile agent app; portal-origin replies seem fine.

When first_response_at is non-null the banner and the sla_state=breached badge should both clear. Instead the banner stays and the queue list still paints the ticket crimson even though the detail pane shows a first response timestamp.

Working theory: the banner query joins on the first public comment's created_at rather than the denormalized first_response_at column. Mobile replies write first_response_at through a different code path that does not also insert a "public" comment flag the join expects, so the breach view keeps matching.
comments: Pulled 47 open triage tickets with first_response_at set; 11 still render the breach banner, all answered from the iOS agent build.
Will patch the banner predicate to prefer first_response_at and treat public comments as a fallback only.

issues.summary: Billing portal shows an unpaid balance after a successful card update
description: After a customer successfully replaces an expired card in the billing portal, the account summary still shows an unpaid balance equal to the last failed invoice amount. Stripe confirms the new payment method and the retry charge succeeds; only our portal balance widget is wrong.

Expected: balance_due cents drop to 0 and the "Payment past due" alert disappears once invoice status becomes paid. Actual: GET /billing/summary keeps returning the pre-update balance_due for several hours even though invoices list the charge as paid.

Hypothesis: the summary endpoint caches balance_due keyed only by tenant_id with a 6-hour TTL, while the card-update webhook refreshes the invoices collection cache but never busts the summary key. Stale balance wins until the TTL expires or someone hits a forced refresh admin action.
Support is fielding NMS tickets from finance contacts who think the charge failed twice. One account attempted a second card update unnecessarily.
comments: Reproduced on staging by failing an invoice, updating the card via portal, then reading /billing/summary before the 6h TTL.
