Webhook handler now invalidates billing:summary:{tenant_id} when payment_method.updated or invoice.paid fires.
Checked three affected tenants after deploy; balance_due flipped to 0 within one request. Closing.

issues.summary: Escalation template variables render as raw placeholders in outbound email
description: Outbound escalation emails are leaving the system with unsubstituted tokens such as {{ticket.subject}} and {{assignee.display_name}} in the body. Recipients on two NMS accounts forwarded screenshots of the raw placeholders.
Template preview inside the admin UI renders correctly. The failure is isolated to the mailer that sends when an escalation is created or severity changes.

Suspected root: the new Markdown template compiler returns a structured AST, but the SMTP adapter still calls the old string-replace helper that only understood {{key}} patterns on a flat map. Variable names nested under ticket.* never get walked, so the placeholders pass through untouched.
Customer-facing impact is high — external stakeholders receive broken notices and lose confidence in the escalation channel.
comments: Diffed preview vs send paths: preview uses TemplateRenderer.v2, send still pipes through LegacyPlaceholderSwap.
Patch in flight to run the same AST walk before MessageBuilder. Will add a golden-file test with nested ticket and assignee fields.

issues.summary: Customer report of data-loss after bulk archive cannot be reproduced in staging
description: A customer claims that bulk-archiving ~120 closed tickets from their portal removed three tickets that still had open child tasks, and those tickets no longer appear in search or recycle bin. They provided ticket keys NMS-44102 through NMS-44104.

We cannot reproduce the loss in staging: bulk archive with the same payload only soft-deletes eligible closed tickets and leaves anything with open children untouched. Staging search still returns the three keys after the same UI steps.

Need a production-only investigation path: audit log for bulk_archive on that tenant around 2026-07-28 14:10 UTC, plus a check whether the archive job's eligibility filter ran against a stale read replica that still showed child tasks as done.
Until we confirm or rule out hard deletion this stays needs-repro; do not mark data-loss confirmed without production evidence.
comments: Asked the customer for the exact agent email that triggered bulk archive and a HAR of the portal session. No reply yet.

issues.summary: Support CSAT survey link expires before the configured 14-day window
description: CSAT survey tokens are dying well before the workspace's 14-day window. Customers who open the link on day 6–9 of a closed ticket often land on "This survey is no longer available." Workspace setting csat_link_ttl_days is explicitly 14.
Expected lifetime is first_response_or_resolve_time + 14 days. Observed lifetime from token issued_at to reject is closer to 5 days on production.

Likely bug: token minting stores expires_at as issued_at + workspace.default_session_ttl_hours (currently 120h) instead of reading csat_link_ttl_days. Session TTL was tightened last release for security and accidentally shortened survey links.
NMS volume: about 30 bounce-backs tagged csat-expired in the last week from customers who meant to complete the survey.
comments: Confirmed expires_at on three sample tokens equals issued_at + 120h, ignoring csat_link_ttl_days=14.
Fix should mint with days from the CSAT setting and leave session TTL alone.

issues.summary: Triage filter for unassigned tickets includes tickets with a temporary owner
description: The triage queue filter "Unassigned only" still returns tickets that have a temporary owner (owner_type=temp_agent from the overflow rotation). Agents using that filter to pick up free work keep grabbing tickets that already have a short-lived assignee.
Expected: only tickets where assignee_id IS NULL. Actual: the filter treats temp_agent ownership as unassigned because the legacy SQL clause was assignee_id IS NULL OR owner_type <> 'agent'.

Hypothesis: when temporary ownership landed, owner_type gained temp_agent but the unassigned filter was never updated to treat temp_agent like a real owner. The UI badge shows the temp name while the filter still classifies the row as free.
Leads report wasted reassignment churn on the APAC triage queue during peak hours.
comments: Updated the filter predicate to require assignee_id IS NULL AND owner_type IS NULL.
QA replayed the APAC queue snapshot: temp-owned tickets no longer appear under Unassigned. Merged and deployed.

issues.summary: Billing refund request form rejects valid VAT IDs from certain EU countries
description: The billing refund request form rejects VAT IDs that pass VIES for several EU countries — notably IE (Ireland), AT (Austria), and EL (Greece, using the EL prefix rather than GR). German and French IDs validate fine.

Customers enter a well-formed ID such as IE6388047V or EL123456789; the form shows "Invalid VAT ID format" before any network call. Expected: client pattern accepts the country-specific shape, then server confirms via VIES.

Root cause was a client regex that assumed every EU VAT ID is [A-Z]{2}[0-9]{8,12}. Irish IDs include a letter check digit and Greek IDs use EL, neither of which the regex allowed. Server-side validator was already correct; only the browser gate was wrong.
Blocked legitimate refund filings from at least five NMS billing contacts last month.
comments: Expanded the client patterns using the same country table the server already ships.
Manually submitted IE, AT, and EL samples on staging; all reach the VIES step now. Closed after prod smoke.

issues.summary: Escalation chat transcript export truncates the last 20 messages
description: Exporting an escalation chat transcript as PDF or CSV always drops the final ~20 messages even when the live transcript pane shows them. Longer threads (90+ messages) make the gap obvious; short threads under ~25 messages export empty tails or cut mid-conversation.
Agents need the full record for handoff and compliance. Export should include every message up to export_requested_at.

Cause: the exporter paginated with LIMIT 50 and a forward cursor, then concatenated pages, but the final page used an off-by-one on the exclusive end cursor (message_id < last_seen instead of <=). The last page's newest 20 rows were systematically excluded when the remainder class was non-zero.
Compliance asked for re-export on two closed escalations after noticing missing resolution chatter.
comments: Wrote a unit test with 73 messages; export previously returned 53. Cursor bound fixed to inclusive end.
Re-exported the two compliance cases; message counts now match the live transcript. Done.

issues.summary: Customer cannot update the contact email on an open billing dispute
description: On an open billing dispute, the contact email field is read-only in the portal even though the help text says the customer can update it while status is open or needs_info. Closed disputes correctly lock the field; open ones should not.
Customers who filed with a shared inbox address cannot redirect notifications to a personal finance alias without calling support to edit the row.
Probable cause: the portal form's canEditContact helper returns true only for status=needs_info and forgot open. API PATCH /disputes/{id}/contact-email already allows open; UI is the sole blocker.

issues.summary: Support knowledge base article links 404 for articles published this week
description: Deep links to knowledge base articles published in the current calendar week return HTTP 404 from the public help host. Older articles (published before Monday 00:00 UTC of the current week) resolve normally.
Agents paste these links into ticket replies; customers hit 404 and reply that the article is missing. CDN purge does not help.

Hypothesis: the public article router resolves slug via a weekly materialized view refreshed by a Monday cron. Articles inserted after the last refresh exist in the authoring DB and internal preview but are absent from the view the public edge queries.
Workaround is linking the internal preview URL, which is undesirable for customers.
comments: Checked publish timestamps: four articles from Wed–Fri this week 404; last week's set is fine. Cron job kb_public_mv_refresh last success was Monday 00:05 UTC.

issues.summary: Triage priority auto-suggest marks every security mention as Highest
description: Triage priority auto-suggest upgrades any ticket whose body or subject contains the substring "security" to Highest, including phrases like "security deposit refund" and "security group misconfiguration for a staging VPC." Real security incidents should still rank high; billing and infra noise should not.

Expected: auto-suggest uses the security_incident classifier score (>0.82) rather than a bare keyword. Actual: a case-insensitive contains("security") short-circuit runs before the model and forces Highest.

That short-circuit was added during a sev-0 drill and never gated behind the classifier. Removing or narrowing it restores model-based suggestions while keeping an allowlist for phrases like "security breach" and "unauthorized access."
Queue leads spent extra time demoting false Highest tickets during Monday triage.
comments: Deleted the keyword short-circuit and added regression fixtures for "security deposit" vs "security breach."
Shadow-scored last week's triage intake: false Highest rate on security-substring tickets dropped from 41% to 3%. Shipped.

issues.summary: Billing double-charge complaint cannot link to the matching invoice ID
description: When filing a billing double-charge complaint, agents cannot attach the matching invoice ID from the search picker. Typing a known invoice number such as inv_7c18a9 returns "No invoices found" even though the same ID opens correctly from the billing admin page.

Expected: picker queries invoices for the ticket's tenant and lets the agent bind invoice_id on the complaint record. Actual: the picker always searches the agent's home workspace tenant, not the ticket customer tenant, so cross-tenant billing tickets never resolve IDs.
Likely a missing tenant_id query param on GET /billing/invoices/search when invoked from the complaint form; the admin page passes it explicitly.
comments: Confirmed in network panel: complaint form omits tenant_id, admin page sends it. Fix queued for next billing sprint.

issues.summary: Escalation on-call page mute suppresses all channels instead of SMS only
description: On the escalation on-call page, choosing "Mute SMS for this shift" also silences Slack and email pages. Engineers who only wanted to stop SMS during a meeting missed Slack page storms and email digests.

Mute should flip sms_muted=true on the shift record and leave slack_muted / email_muted unchanged. Observed: the toggle writes muted_channels=["sms","slack","email"] because the UI reuses the "mute all" payload shape with a single boolean.
Backend already supports per-channel flags; only the on-call settings form collapses them.

issues.summary: Customer sees another tenant workspace name briefly on portal load
description: For a brief moment after hard-loading the customer portal, the header shows another tenant's workspace display name before swapping to the correct one. Duration is usually 200–600 ms; long enough for a screenshot and a security-conscious customer to file an NMS ticket.

Expected: never paint a workspace name that does not belong to the authenticated session. Actual: first paint uses a cached shell value from localStorage key nimbus.portal.lastWorkspaceLabel without checking it against the session tenant_id.
Cross-tenant label flash is a confidentiality concern even if ticket bodies never leak. Session bootstrap should either wait for /me or clear the label when tenant_id mismatches.
comments: Reproduced with two test accounts in different workspaces on the same browser profile; localStorage retained the previous label.
Guarded the shell to blank the label until /me returns and to wipe lastWorkspaceLabel on tenant mismatch.

Reopened: customer on tenant_id tnt_88c still saw "Acme Robotics Staging" flash this morning after our fix. They use a shared device kiosk; investigating whether service worker is caching the old shell HTML.

issues.summary: Support reply drafts autosave overwrites concurrent agent edits
description: When two agents open the same support reply draft, autosave from agent A overwrites agent B's newer keystrokes without merge or conflict UI. Last writer before the 8-second autosave interval wins; the other agent's paragraph disappears on next poll.

Expected: either operational transform / CRDT merge, or a conflict banner when revision tokens diverge. Actual: PUT /drafts/{id} is last-write-wins with no If-Match check, and the client blindly replaces local state with the server body on poll.
Hypothesis: revision field exists on the draft row but neither the autosave client nor the API enforces it. Concurrent edits during shift overlap (common on Sev-1 threads) silently drop text.
Already lost a carefully worded legal reply once; agent had to reconstruct from memory.
comments: Added If-Match on draft updates; API returns 409 with both revisions when tokens differ.
Client still auto-applies server body on 200 poll — working on a merge banner next.
Reopened after prod: two agents on ticket NMS-55210 both hit autosave within the same second; one paragraph still vanished. 409 path is not wired for the poll path, only for explicit save.

issues.summary: Triage backlog count includes spam tickets marked for deletion
description: The triage backlog badge count includes tickets already marked spam_pending_deletion. Those rows are hidden from the default queue list but still inflate the number next to "Backlog," so leads think the queue is larger than what agents can see.
Count should match the default list filter: exclude status=spam_pending_deletion and deleted_at IS NOT NULL. Current count query only filters deleted_at, so spam marked for purge remains.
No customer data issue — pure operator confusion — but it drives unnecessary overtime requests on Monday mornings.

issues.summary: Billing question about seat reduction is auto-closed after 48 hours of silence
description: Billing questions whose subject or category is seat reduction are auto-closed by the silence bot after 48 hours without a customer reply, even when an agent is waiting on finance approval and has posted an internal note. Other billing categories use the standard 7-day silence window.

Expected: seat-reduction questions follow the same 7-day policy as refund and invoice disputes, or at least respect snooze / waiting_on_internal. Actual: a dedicated rule seat_reduction_silence_hours=48 closes the ticket and sends a "we assume this is resolved" email.
That rule was a temporary measure during a pricing launch and was never removed. Customers re-open or file duplicates when finance finally answers.
comments: Product confirmed the 48h rule should be retired; tracking config change plus a one-line bot update.

issues.summary: Escalation secondary assignee is not notified when the primary is out of office
description: When the primary escalation assignee has an active out-of-office calendar block, the secondary assignee never receives the reassignment or page notification. The ticket shows secondary on the roster but notification_log has no rows for that user.

Expected: OOO on primary triggers notify_secondary with the same channels the primary would have received. Actual: the OOO handler only unassigns primary and leaves secondary without an event, so nobody is paged until a human notices.
Likely gap in the OOO workflow step: it updates assignee_id but skips the NotificationFanout call that create-escalation uses for secondaries.

issues.summary: Add macros for common billing proration explanations
description: Billing agents retype the same proration explanations on a large share of seat-change and plan-switch tickets. We need shared macros so answers stay consistent and audits can cite a macro_id.

Deliver three macros in the billing library: mid-cycle seat increase, mid-cycle seat decrease with credit, and annual-to-monthly switch proration. Each macro should pull {{invoice.next_amount}}, {{proration.credit_cents}}, and {{period.end_date}} from the billing context. Done when macros appear under Billing → Proration and pass a dry-run render against fixture tenant tnt_macros_01.
comments: Drafted copy for seat increase and decrease; still waiting on finance wording for annual-to-monthly.
Increase/decrease macros merged to staging macro pack. Building the annual switch variant with the credit line finance approved yesterday.

issues.summary: Document the escalation path for data-loss customer reports
description: When a customer reports possible data-loss, agents currently improvise the escalation path. We need a single internal doc that states severity defaults, who to page, evidence to collect, and when to involve infra versus application on-call.

Completion: a published runbook under Support Ops → Escalation titled "Customer data-loss reports," linked from the escalation create form's help popover, covering intake checklist, severity matrix (including when to use Sev-1), communication templates, and post-incident ticket hygiene. Review sign-off from Escalation leads required before marking done.

issues.summary: Backfill missing first_response_at timestamps on closed triage tickets
description: About 2,300 closed triage tickets from before the first_response_at backfill job are missing that timestamp even though they have a clear first public agent comment. SLA reporting excludes them or treats them as never-responded.

Done when a one-shot migration sets first_response_at from the earliest public agent comment for closed tickets where the column is null, writes a dry-run report of row counts per week, and leaves open tickets untouched for the live writer path. Include a reversible backup table triage_first_response_backfill_2026q2.
comments: Dry-run counted 2,287 rows; sample of 50 matched comment timestamps manually.
Migration ran in production during the Tuesday maintenance window; spot-checked SLA dashboard — null first_response_at on closed triage is now under 20 legacy rows with no public comments.

issues.summary: Create a runbook for verifying portal SSO after IdP certificate rotation
description: After IdP certificate rotations, portal SSO breakages show up as a spike in NMS login tickets. Engineers re-derive the verification steps from memory; we need a durable runbook.

Ship a runbook that covers: confirming the new x509 in the IdP metadata URL, updating the portal SSO cert PEM in admin, purging the metadata cache key sso:idp_meta:{workspace_id}, running the /auth/sso/self-check endpoint, and a five-minute canary with a test user. Include rollback (restore previous PEM) and who to page if self-check fails in production.

issues.summary: Add CSAT response export for the previous billing quarter
description: Finance wants CSAT responses for the previous billing quarter exported as CSV for the board pack. Today agents can only screenshot dashboards or page through the UI.

Done: an export job on the CSAT admin page filtered by response_submitted_at within the selected quarter, columns for ticket_id, score, comment, queue, and billing_account_id, delivered as a downloadable CSV and optionally emailed to the requester. Verified against Q1 fixture data (1,042 rows) matching the dashboard aggregate.
comments: Implemented export with quarter picker; Q1 fixture row count matches dashboard 1042.
Finance confirmed the CSV columns on a dry run. Closing.

issues.summary: Wire support portal audit logs into the shared SIEM pipeline
description: Support portal audit events (login, dispute filed, contact email change, invoice download) currently sit only in the application Postgres audit table. Security wants them in the shared SIEM pipeline alongside app and API logs.

Wire the existing audit publisher to emit portal events to the SIEM HTTPS intake with fields actor_id, tenant_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, ip, and user_agent. Acceptance: staging SIEM shows portal.login and portal.dispute.create within 60 seconds of the action, with a runbook snippet for on-call to query them. No change to customer-visible portal behavior.
comments: Mapped action names to the SIEM schema; need a secrets grant for the intake token in staging before enabling the publisher flag.

issues.summary: Remove retired escalation severity values from the admin UI
description: Admin UI for escalation severity still lists retired values Sev-0-legacy and experimental-p1 that the API no longer accepts on create. Saving a policy that includes them returns 422 and confuses workspace admins.

Remove retired values from the severity multiselect and from the default policy templates. Keep read-only display for historical escalations that still store those codes. Done when the admin form only offers active severities from GET /escalations/severities?status=active and a screenshot checklist is attached for docs.
comments: Active-only fetch is in a draft PR; need design review on how historical rows render in the severity column.
Design signed off on a muted badge for retired codes on old records. Finishing the form filter next.

issues.summary: Add Playwright coverage for the billing question multi-step form
description: The billing question multi-step form (category → account picker → details → review) has no Playwright coverage and has regressed twice in the last quarter on step validation.

Add a Playwright spec that walks a happy path for category=invoice_discrepancy, asserts step guards when required fields are empty, submits successfully against mocked billing APIs, and checks the confirmation screen shows the new ticket key. Wire it into CI's support-portal project. Done when the spec is green in CI three consecutive main builds.

issues.summary: Write agent training notes for workspace merge support scenarios
description: Workspace merge support scenarios (two tenants combining billing and ticket history) generate high-severity NMS threads, but agents lack a single training note describing what merges preserve, what customers must do, and common failure replies.

Deliver an internal training note covering pre-merge checklist, post-merge ticket visibility rules, billing invoice ownership, and three sample reply macros. Publish under Agent Academy → Advanced and link from the triage playbook. Done when L&D marks the note required reading for tier-2 agents.
comments: Draft reviewed by billing and triage leads; incorporated the invoice ownership section.
Published and added to the tier-2 required list. Closing.

issues.summary: Normalize ticket source tags between portal and email intake
description: Tickets created from the portal use source=portal while email intake uses source=email_inbound, but several reports and macros still look for the legacy tags web and mail. Mixed tags break automation that routes portal tickets to the self-serve queue.

Normalize on portal and email as the only stored source values; migrate existing web→portal and mail→email_inbound rows; update macros and report definitions. Completion criteria: zero open tickets with legacy tags, and the intake dual-write removed after one release of read-compatible mapping.
comments: Inventory found 18 macros and 4 saved reports still filtering on web/mail.
Migration script ready for staging; dual-write mapper is in review so old clients keep working during the cutover.

issues.summary: Add a weekly report of SLA breaches by queue for managers
description: Managers currently export SLA breach CSVs by hand each Monday. They want an automated weekly report grouped by queue.

Build a scheduled report that runs Monday 06:00 workspace time, lists breach counts and median minutes past SLA per queue for the prior 7 days, and emails subscribed managers a CSV plus a short HTML summary. Done when two pilot queues (Billing Questions and Triage) receive correct numbers for a shadow week matching the manual export within 1%.

issues.summary: Migrate legacy support macros off the deprecated template engine
description: Sixty-one support macros still compile on the deprecated Mustache-like engine scheduled for removal next quarter. New macros already use the Handlebars-compatible engine; mixed runtimes complicate variable docs.

Migrate remaining macros to the new engine, fix variables that relied on implicit HTML escaping differences, and delete the legacy renderer flag. Done when macro_runtime=legacy count is 0 in production and the deprecation banner is removed from the macro editor.
comments: Converted 22 of 61 macros; billing pack is next because it uses nested invoice fields the old engine treated as flat.
Hit one escaping difference on HTML links inside macros — documenting the new triple-stash pattern for agents mid-migration.

issues.summary: Document customer-facing language for rate limit related outages
description: When rate limiting causes partial outages, agents invent different customer-facing explanations, some of which over-promise timelines or imply a full platform down. We need approved language.

Publish a short internal guide with: what customers may observe (429s, delayed webhooks), safe wording for status updates, what not to say (no root-cause speculation), and links to the status page component for API rate limits. Done when Support Comms and SRE both approve and the guide is linked from the incident bridge checklist.

issues.summary: Create fixtures for escalation timer tests across timezones
description: Escalation timer unit tests assume the process timezone is UTC, so failures appear for engineers in US/Pacific and Asia/Seoul. We need fixtures that pin zones explicitly.

Add shared fixtures covering timer start/stop across UTC, America/New_York, and Asia/Tokyo, including a DST spring-forward boundary for New York. Done when the escalation timer suite passes with TZ set to each of those values in CI matrix jobs.
comments: Fixtures landed; CI matrix now runs the timer package under three TZ values.
One flaky assertion around relative "business hours" fixed by freezing clock at 2026-03-08 01:30 America/New_York. All green — closing.

issues.summary: Add a dashboard tile for open billing disputes older than 7 days
description: Billing leads lack a at-a-glance signal for disputes stuck open longer than a week. They currently filter the disputes table manually.

Add a manager dashboard tile "Open billing disputes > 7 days" showing count and a drill-down list sorted by age. Data source: disputes where status IN (open, needs_info) and opened_at < now() - interval 7 days. Acceptance: tile matches a manual SQL count on staging for tenant tnt_dash_demo, refreshes at most every 5 minutes, and respects the viewer's workspace scope.
comments: Product wants the tile on the Billing overview dashboard only, not the global home. Adjusting placement before implementation.
